### Compare showed two pictures where the record belonged

⚠️ **`.cmpcards` expected `.dcard` children and got bare divs**, so the column layout and every rule under `.dcard.lc` — twelve classes — styled nothing. The cards render the **record** now, laid out so two of them line up field for field: the attachment list is the thing you actually compare, and reading it out of two Discord renders means reading two pictures. The Discord render did not go away — it lives in the build editor's own side column, beside the fields that produce it, where it costs no request per picked build.

### The instrument needed one more correction

`portalCoverage`'s shared set mirrors the mockup's `docs/superpowers/mockups/2026-08-23-portal-interactive/assets/shell.js` — what every page shares — and `Shell.Export` is declared there, so every realm's *want* carries the export panel's vocabulary. Attributing the portal's `exportPanel.js` per realm made those classes read as missing from **Door**, which renders no realm surfaces at all and cannot be given one. Moving it lifts Door 70% → 78% and changes no markup. `manifest.js` and `oneway.js` deliberately stay per-realm: the mockup declares both in its shell too, but Home and Door render neither, and counting them shared would inflate exactly the realms this correction exists to stop mis-measuring.

**Coverage 71% → 80% (Season 73% → 84%, Armory 61% → 76%, Broadcast 74% → 80%, Analytics 80% → 85%, Door 70% → 78%), orphans 0, and the round trip is demonstrated rather than asserted**: exporting the fixture armory and pasting the result back reads as *2 update, 0 new*.

**Creation reached the masthead on every realm that has it, and the shortcut is written on the button.** Measured on this branch: Armory's and Broadcast's only "new" affordance was a command-palette entry plus a button inside the Bulk view, and Access's grant form sat at the foot of a grid — the one thing an admin opens the portal to *do* was reachable only by already knowing where it was. `Shell.MastheadNew` is one control shared by all four, and it binds its own access key **and renders it**, from the same value, so the two cannot drift; the binding ignores the keystroke while a text field has focus, because a bare letter is a character before it is a shortcut. Access's button travels to the form and focuses the field rather than revealing a second copy — two grant forms can disagree, and one of them would be wrong.

**The composer now says what it is about to create.** It has drawn a ghost onto the Track since the Track was built, which answers *where*; nothing answered *what*, so a name typo and a mis-picked type were both invisible until after staging. The preview renders genuinely empty when there is nothing true to say, because the adopted sheet hides it with `:empty` and a "nothing yet" placeholder would reserve 76px of the composer forever.

**Home stopped being unable to answer the portal's own question.** The attention list says what is *wrong* and the clock says how long the season has; neither said what a player opening the bot this second would be shown. "Running right now" and "Showing to players" answer exactly that, and they re-use `seasonItems` rather than filtering again — Home has already been burned twice by holding its own copy of a predicate and disagreeing with the realm it links to. The staged-work strip offers the way back to Review and deliberately does **not** carry "Discard all": Review is the only screen that commits, and discarding everything from a summary strip that lists none of it is the one shape of that button nobody should press.

**Access's scope grid says which scopes reach the portal at all.** Eleven tokens, and whether one is a portal realm or Discord-only lived in a `title` attribute — a hover, on a row being read with the eyes. A scope with no holder besides the owner now reads *"nobody but you"* in quiet ink rather than sharing the warning colour with *"single point"*: sole ownership is the resting state of a solo-maintained bot, and a mark that fires on the common case is a mark readers learn to skip. The permission drawer splits granting from revoking into groups coloured by direction — they had been two identical bold paragraphs describing opposite acts — and states the operation id the server will actually see.

**Broadcast previews the message, not the records.** It is the one realm whose output a player reads verbatim, and the accent colour, the delivery order and the embed cap were three separate facts on screen adding up to something shown nowhere. Anything past the cap is *absent* from the preview rather than greyed out, because a player does not see a faded row.

Two of these were closed yesterday; **a gate is a claim about what it can see, and a regex that cannot nest claims less than it appears to.**

The percentage floors now, and an exact `100%` is reserved for `have === want`, so the top of the scale cannot lie. ⚠️ **The framing of this release is worth stating plainly, because the number invites the wrong lesson.** The story is not that coverage went 85% → 1493/1495. The number is a side effect. **Work that started from "what is this surface FOR" was consistently good; work that started from "which class is missing" was mixed** — one design error, one probably-redundant panel, two unverified changes. A future session should walk the list and let it choose the QUESTION, never the answer.

⚠️ **THE CORRECT RULE WAS NEVER MISSING, AND THAT IS THE ACTUAL LESSON.** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is auto-loaded into every session, states the flag rule with its own measurement, and **names `local/` explicitly**; `usage-guard.mjs` fires the same advice as a live hook and fired it repeatedly during the session that finally caught this. **The repo-local claim won anyway, for months, across ~17 documents.** A false SPECIFIC claim beats a true GENERAL rule because it is camouflaged as an **exception** to it — *"these particular files are unreachable"* reads as domain knowledge from someone who checked, not as a contradiction, so the general rule is left intact and quietly overridden. 🔴 **When a document says a rule you already hold does not apply here, test the EXCEPTION rather than the rule** — it is the higher-variance claim and this one cost a single command. And repetition is not corroboration: seventeen copies of one untested sentence is one source. Filed as the memory `feedback_false_tool_reach_claims`.

🔴 **The cost was concrete.** Told the exhaustive records were unsearchable, sessions did not search them, so every residual list was assembled from the tracked subset and came back confidently incomplete — **five design items existed only there**, and locating the gap took three forced `sequentialthinking` passes at Harkirat's insistence. **A false claim about a tool's reach is self-sealing: acting on it produces exactly the evidence that confirms it.**

A reader doing exactly what the section trains them to do — test the claim — would have seen it refuted and concluded the opposite of the truth. **A probe quoted in a tracked document stops being a valid probe;** it is replaced by a command plus an invariant SHAPE (`0 · 0 · non-zero`), with the probe declared disposable and the reason stated. The second blocker was two different counts of the same thing inside one file, reconciling with neither reality — replaced by the structural rule, which needs no maintenance.

🔴 **AND THE FIRST VERSION CLONED THE COMPONENT IT SHOULD HAVE REUSED — a duplicate `.lvlbars`/`.lvlb` block, 2,400 lines above the original, with the same selectors and different values.** The daily-bar charts were then styled by whichever definition the cascade happened to reach last: measured on the page, `Alerts per day` and `Commands per day` had swapped to the new geometry. ⚠️ **`portal:orphans` passed the whole time** — it asks whether a class has a rule, and both had several. **A duplicate selector is invisible to every gate here.** The new panel now reuses the component and adds only three level tints, beside the rules they modify.

⚠️ **Two more caught by gates the repo already had, both mine.** A backtick inside an HTML comment inside a template literal (the build refuses it by name — third time on this branch), and a line ending immediately before an inline `<b>`, which htm collapses into a run-on word: the same defect fixed in Armory's Coverage sentence earlier the same day, and there is a test for it that named the two lines.

**And the Track — the thing the Track tab exists to show — was the SIXTH block on it.** Measured at 1280: you clicked *Track* and the ruler began **863px below the tab**, behind the identity strip, a 126px draft card and a 438px staged-changes callout. That callout's own comment says the mockup keeps pending changes *"right beside the Track"* — the intent was adjacency and the execution was obstruction. It now sits below, where it is still beside it. **Ruler at y=1266 → y=761.**

**Two deadlines on one date were being asserted three separate times, one screen from a panel that modelled them correctly.** Battle Pass and Ranked both end Sep 10. The rail drew a chip each, stacked them on two rows over one line with two stems to the same x, and then drew a `.dnotch` beneath them saying the date was shared — while the season clock in the masthead already read `UNTIL SEP 10 · BATTLE PASS · RANKED`. Two labels for one moment is a **modelling error**, so the model changed: group by date *before* the rows are packed, one chip carrying both names with a key dot each. The notch had nothing left to say and is gone. The test that asserted the old behaviour — *"two deadlines on the same day take different rows"* — had been passing for exactly as long as the defect existed; it now asserts the merge, with a falsifier proving deadlines on *different* days still separate.

🔴 **`--xtop` and `.dflag.flip` were both consumers with no producer, and each had been silently doing nothing since the migration.** `--xtop` is read by `.xhair::before` and `.xd` and was set by no code anywhere, so the crosshair's date bubble used its hard-coded `60px` fallback forever — the exact defect the mockup records as fixed. `.dflag.flip` was worse: the rule was scoped `.dend .dflag.flip`, and `.dend` is the vertical **line on the overlay**, not the rail — the same never-matching selector the mockup documents against its own `fitFlags()`, ported here along with the rule, *and* no code added the class. Both halves were needed: merging the two Sep 10 chips into one 205px box pushed it **10px past the plot's right edge**, where `overflow-x:clip` ate part of the date. **`--xtop` is now measured rather than summed** — the first version added up the scrub, the ruler and the rail, forgot the overview strip, and landed 60px wrong, which is why a fourth copy of three existing measurements is not a fix.

**Two draws dated Aug 22 drew two diamonds at one coordinate, and the second one did not exist as far as the page was concerned** — no hover, no focus, no tooltip, no way to reach it. `clusterPoints` was in the mockup, the CSS for it (`.ptc.mark.stack`, `.pt.hid`, the same-day ring) was already in the stylesheet, and the JS that would emit any of it was never ported. It branches on the **fact, not the pixel condition that triggered it**: *"2 releases on Aug 22 — the same day, so zooming will not separate them"*, because the alternative sentence asks for something no zoom can do.

**And the pin was never on the rail's layout at all.** A pin ("DMZ NOV 11 · 53d beyond this view") welded to the edge in a rail fixed at 52px, so it painted through the Ranked flag. The first fix was wrong in an instructive way: a pin is **bottom-anchored** where a flag is top-anchored, so giving it a flag's `level` lifted it *toward* the flags — measured, worse than the collision. Pins stack among pins; clearing the flags is the rail's job, and `railBox()` derives the height from the rows actually used. **Three duplicate or dead stylesheet blocks went with it**: a second `.pt.hid`, a `.ptc.same` declared 1,700 lines from its family and painting a second ring over the first, and the retired notch.

⚠️ **Every one of these was invisible to the whole gate set.** `npm test`, `portal:orphans`, `portal:coverage` and `portal:refs` were green throughout — they ask whether a class has a rule and whether a function has a test, never whether two elements on one screen agree. What found them was a **relational** probe: for each pair of rail chips, do their boxes intersect; for each pair of points in a lane, are they within 17px. Both report **zero** now, from four and one.

**The two dead calendar banners are re-hosted, and the fix took a fresh source rather than a script.** `drawsBannerUrl` and `eventsBannerUrl` were `media.discordapp.net` links with expired `ex=` signatures — they rendered as nothing in Discord and nothing in the portal, and no script could repair them because re-hosting needs a source and the sources were gone. Harkirat supplied two fresh signed URLs; both went through `utils/calendarBannerCache.js`, the mechanism that has been correct since 2026-08-07 and was only ever waiting on an input, and landed at the same two stable public ids. **Both databases now point at Cloudinary** — prod and the local dev database, the second of which matters because the dev bot and the dev portal read it and would otherwise still render dead links. All three banners can now no longer expire.

**And the pending list turned out to be wrong twice in one evening, in the same way both times.** Asked what remained, the answer was assembled from the two most recent trackers and missed the two documents that actually hold it: the completion plan's own **A–S inventory**, and — the one Harkirat meant — the **pre-migration design list** in a gitignored handoff, which a default `rg` cannot see. His correction was the same one he had already given once before: *"you forgetting ALL the stuff that's still originally pending??"* **The remedy is structural rather than a resolution to try harder**: the new plan names its six sources and instructs that the list be assembled by reading them, never by remembering.

🔴 **THE MIGRATION CARRIED THE STYLESHEET AND DROPPED THE MARKUP THAT ACTIVATES IT — and that single sentence explains a class of defect nobody could see.** Harkirat: *"idk what you were using as reference during the migration but you did not stay true to the mockup design and somehow broke the same things we had already fixed."* Literally true, and it has a mechanism. **Measured on the running page: the command bar's input renders at 44px inside a 34px wrapper, each painting its own background and its own border** — the doubled search bar, fixed weeks ago, back. The fix is still in the stylesheet: `:not([data-bare])` opts an input out of the global form reset, and **no file in `portal/ui/` emits the attribute.** Two more of the same shape were found and fixed the same evening — `--xtop` was read by two rules and set by no code, so the crosshair used its hard-coded fallback forever; `.dflag.flip` had a rule scoped to the wrong parent *and* no writer. **A rule with no matching element is silent forever, and every gate here asks the opposite question**: `portal:orphans` asks whether a class has a rule, `portal:coverage` counts emitted classes, `npm test` renders components and reads their output. A first reverse sweep — does this *rule* have an *element*? — reported three orphaned `data-` attributes, three custom properties read but never set, and 48 classes with rules and no emitter, among them **Armory's four tier classes and Home's entire card system**.

**The plan that replaces all of this is one document, and it argues with itself in public.** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-portal-conformance.md` supersedes the completion plan and folds its A–S inventory in **re-verified rather than copied** — that inventory had marked the search bar fixed on the same day it was measurably broken. Its falsification pass ran twice, thirty `sequentialthinking` thoughts, and the second round found that the first draft **compared two fixture renderings and called that conformance** while the artifact Harkirat actually uses — the real portal, real Mongo, real OAuth — had never been looked at; that it **shipped nothing he could look at**, despite his acceptance test being visual; and that it had missed **five entire bodies of work**, including a UX-copy audit that had never been folded into any plan and a login page that appears in none of its parts. Seventeen findings, each recorded with what it would have cost.

⚠️ **`kind: plan` now accepts `status: live`, and the exception is deliberate.** Every plan here had been a frozen snapshot, which is right for a plan written once and then executed and wrong for one that tracks its own execution. Harkirat asked for a plan that *"never accidentally goes out of sync."* Forcing it to `frozen` would have made the document lie about its own tense contract — the exact failure the field exists to prevent, pointing the other way. **`spec` deliberately did not gain it**: a dated design snapshot is superseded by a new one, never edited.

**Light mode was never decided, and now it is.** Measured: `prefers-color-scheme` and `data-theme` appear **zero times** in the portal's two stylesheets — it was dark-only by omission, while a tracker row carried *"light mode has never been checked at desktop width"*, a row describing a surface that does not exist and inviting a future session to build one uninvited. It surfaced only because a dimension no inventory listed was checked at all. Harkirat's answer: **dark-only is deliberate.** The row is retired with its original text kept, per the conservation rule.

🔴 **THE GATE THAT ASKED THE OTHER QUESTION — and it found the doubled search bar in its first run.** Part 0 of the conformance plan built the inverse of `portal:orphans`: not *does this class have a rule*, but **does this rule have an element**. `scripts/portalReverseOrphans.mjs` looks for four shapes — a `[data-*]` selector with no emitter, a `var(--x)` read with no setter anywhere, a class with two or more rules and no emitter, and a **name mismatch**, where the class IS emitted and no rule matches it. That last shape is why it parses expressions instead of grepping: `armory.js` emits its tier rows from a lookup table, so a literal-prefix scanner reports the prefix as an orphan, calls the one working class unemitted, and stays silent about the four rows that really are broken — three wrong answers from one missing capability, and it is a miss that had already happened twice. First run: **4 dead data attributes, 3 unset custom properties, 101 styled-and-unemitted classes, and 6 name mismatches**, including the three Armory tier rows emitting `t-t3`/`t-t4`/`t-t5` against a stylesheet that defines `.t-top3`/`.t-top4`/`.t-top5`. ⚠️ **It prints its own blind spot rather than hiding it** — 24 class expressions resolve to a variable built elsewhere, so a finding behind one of those may be a false positive, and `--why <class>` names the emitting file in one command. That is how a class with 74 rules turned out to be emitted after all.

**The doubled search bar is fixed, and the fix is one attribute.** `[data-bare]` opts an input out of the global form reset, the reset carries four `:not()` attribute clauses that put it at specificity 0,4,1, and the `.cmdbar input.cb-in` rule written to override it sits at 0,2,1 — so the override has been losing the argument silently. **Measured before: a 44px input, with its own border, background and radius, inside a 34px bar painting all three. Measured after: 16px, no border, transparent.** An opt-out cannot lose an argument it is not having.

**And the shell diff found a second defect nobody had reported: the portal was printing its own internal ids at readers.** The rail read *"season armory broadcast access analytics"*, the breadcrumb read *"season"*, each realm's panel was titled with its id and the command bar offered *"Search season, or run a command"* — against a mockup whose rail reads *"Season Armory Broadcast"*, and against COMPANION §2307's explicit rule that the word `realm` and its ids stay in the code while anything a person reads names the page. One `REALM_LABEL` map now serves the rail, the crumb, the panel title and the placeholder, because a second copy is how two surfaces come to disagree about what a place is called.

**The instruments the mockup shipped with had never been loaded by any page.** `.grid.js` and `.peers.js` sit beside the eight mockup pages, are copied into the portal's own harness, and **not one mockup page included them** — so `__grid.all()` had never once run on the artifact the portal is measured against, and every comparison so far had measured one side with an instrument and the other by eye. A loader in `docs/superpowers/mockups/2026-08-23-portal-interactive/assets/shell.js` — the one file all eight pages already load, `door.html` included — gives them `?grid` at boot and `__instruments()` on demand. First reading on Season: **1361 elements examined, 2 near-misses, 33 size issues.** The **1282×888 viewport contract** is baked into the same instrument: a page cannot resize its own window, so every reading now carries the size it was taken at, and the geometry runner refuses to record an off-contract one.

**A third defect, found because a registered state could not reach its own subject: "Copy my Discord ID" acknowledged nothing at all.** Both routes to it — the account menu and the command bar — were a bare `navigator.clipboard?.writeText(...)`: no confirmation on success, and in an insecure context or on a refused permission the optional chain swallows the entire action, so a click does nothing and there is no way to tell a silent success from a silent failure. Every other completing action in this portal says so. Both now route through one function that toasts on success and, on refusal, says what to do instead. **Five states had been walking vacuously before that** — one clicked a `role="group"` wrapper instead of the toggle inside it, another matched the first `[role=menuitem]` rather than the one it meant — so each registered state now names the element its own steps are supposed to produce, and a state that does not reach it fails instead of reporting a clean default view under that state's name.

🔴 **THE PORTAL RAN AGAINST REAL DATA FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND THREE THINGS THAT HAD NEVER WORKED CAME OUT AT ONCE.** Harkirat was away from his machine, so the sign-in went through **Discord's QR login** — the QR screenshotted out of the live page, scanned from his phone, authorized in chat. `/api/review`, which the plan records as having *"executed in no environment, ever"*, returned 200 with its ops and changesets on the first request. Everything after that was found in the twenty minutes that followed.

**Every banner edit the Season editor has ever staged was born BLOCKED.** The identity editor keyed its payload on the field the season document STORES (`drawsBannerUrl`); `calendar.setBanners` validates against the page NAMES it accepts (`draws`, `events`, `playlists`). So the op answered *Unknown banner page: drawsBannerUrl*, the changeset went straight to `blocked`, and it could never commit. **Nothing could have caught it:** staging succeeds, and only the Review screen's re-validation ever runs the op against the record again. Two vocabularies for one thing — the same shape as the `t-t4`/`.t-top4` mismatch found the same day, one layer down. A conservation test now reads both lists and fails when they disagree, and it was proven able to fail against the exact key that shipped.

**And the screen that would have told you was throwing the sentence away.** `/api/review` read `failure.reason` — a field no validator sets, because `validateSet` reports `{ index, errors: [...] }` — so the reader was shown *"This change no longer validates"* while the system was holding *"Unknown banner page: drawsBannerUrl"*. The portal's own error rule is that a message names WHAT failed, what it MEANS, and ONE action; the generic form gives a reader none of the three.

🔴 **A change past character 60 disappeared from the diff entirely.** `fmtDiffValue` truncates a long value for display, and `diffRows` compared the TRUNCATED strings — so two Cloudinary URLs identical for their first 60 characters and differing only in the tail read as *no change at all*. A banner edit rendered as an op with **zero rows** on the one screen in the portal that commits: a change you are asked to approve, shown to you as nothing. It compares the raw values now and formats only for display, and a long value keeps its **tail** as well as its head, because the end is where a URL, a filename and a version segment actually differ.

**Two more instruments, both built to be falsified before being trusted.** `scripts/portalGeometry.mjs` records a realm's grid counts *and* its inventory — heading, view tabs, column headers, section headings — because `__grid` reports geometry and not identity: two elements can be perfectly on-grid and be the wrong two. `scripts/portalStates.mjs` walks a registry of states through the harness and runs three **relational** passes: a control drawing a second box inside a wrapper drawn tight around it, content clipped to nothing while holding text, and a control no Tab can reach — plus a "modal" the tab order walks out of. 🔴 **Relational is the entire point.** Every gate this repo had is shaped *for each element, assert something about that element*, and that shape structurally cannot see two elements disagreeing — which is how a 44px input in a 34px wrapper survived weeks of green suites and two human reports. **13 shell states walk clean**, including both door states and the four request failures.

**And the geometry fixture failed its own round-trip the first time it was asked to do one.** `--check` immediately after `--write`, with no code in between, reported `Track · nearMisses: 8 → 4` — a smoke alarm going off when nobody is cooking, and the single fastest way to teach a session to re-record instead of to look. Five readings taken inside one settled page were identical, which located it precisely: the reading was stable, the moment it was taken was not. The first view was measured the instant fonts resolved while every later view got a settle after its tab click. Every view gets the same settle now, and **a reading is only accepted once it repeats** — read, wait, read again, require agreement, and report a surface that never stabilises rather than recording whatever the last attempt happened to see.

⚠️ **Three of these instruments were wrong on their first run, and each correction is now a test.** The reverse sweep reported all seven `.v2-*` classes as unstyled because it read two stylesheets where the build concatenates three. The states walk reported nineteen defects in the account menu that were simply a closed panel measuring zero, and then reported a perfectly ordinary field inside a panel as a doubled box — so PASS 1 now requires the wrapper to be drawn *tight* around the control, since a finding that is wrong three times a run is a finding nobody reads. And the slow-request state failed its own presence check, because the guard asserted on focusable elements and a skeleton legitimately has none. **A probe that cannot report presence cannot be trusted to report absence**, and each of those is pinned by a case that fails when the fix is removed.

### Part 1 — Season, measured against the design surface by surface (2026-08-28)

> 🔴 **THAT HEADING OVERSTATES, AND THE CORRECTION IS ADDED IN PLACE RATHER THAN WRITTEN OVER IT — 2026-08-28 16:5x EDT.** Every individual claim in the paragraphs below is true and every fix in them holds. **Season was not measured surface by surface.** Its COMPOSITION was never compared against the mockup at all: the Track sat 530px below the fold behind a context strip the shell did not have, the panel drew a header duplicating the one 60px above it, and `TL.days` returned NaN on every real record. Harkirat found four such defects in about two seconds by putting two screenshots side by side, immediately after this entry was written.
>
> **The mechanism is worth more than the list:** every instrument this pass mandated enumerates ELEMENTS, so a page with the right elements in the wrong arrangement passes all of them. The remedy is `npm run portal:diff` — render both pages and subtract them — and the full account is in the conformance plan's **§0.44, §0.45 and §0.46**. Season's ledger row was reopened from ☑ to ◐.

**The Manifest had never once been recessive, on any realm.** COMPANION §10.4's composition rule is four bands — masthead, a context strip that is *"a strip, never a panel"*, the view layer with the strongest treatment, and a Manifest that is *"visually recessive… the mechanism beneath the picture"* — and the stylesheet implements that last one in a single adjacent-sibling rule. `shell.js` wrapped each panel in its own `<div>`, so the two panels were never siblings and the rule had never matched anything. Measured on Season at 1282: the view panel and the Manifest both painting `rgb(23,30,36)`, against the mockup's `rgb(23,30,36)` and **transparent**. That is §10.4's own stated failure quoted back at it — *"three panels of identical weight where nothing said which mattered"* — live on all seven realms. The two ids had no rule and no reader anywhere; deleting them fixed the composition everywhere at once.

**A compound selector whose left half is alive is invisible to every gate here.** Season's Repairs styled its finding rows as `.rephits li` while `track.js` renders `.rephits > button` — five rules dead, so every finding lost its padding, its hover, and the type contrast between the item's name and the reason it was flagged. The reverse-orphan sweep cannot see this and should not be expected to: `.rephits` **is** emitted, so the class is not an orphan; only the descendant was. **A sweep that reports classes will never report a dead descendant.**

**The label-fitting pass on the Track was a two-cycle, and the loop ran through the stylesheet.** `nolabel` sets `.bl{display:none}`, and a hidden element reports `scrollWidth: 0` — so the next pass computed that the label needed 10px, found 68px of clear track, and chose `lbl-out`, which shows the label again, which restores `scrollWidth: 169`, which chooses `nolabel`. Measured live from identical geometry: the same 18px bar read `need 10` before a lane collapse and `need 179` after it. `useMeasured.js`'s own header describes exactly this loop as the reason the mockup's version could not be ported; the loop was ported anyway, one indirection further back. The label's natural width now comes from a canvas text measurement, which depends on the string and the font and on nothing the pass can set — and **whether the label is rendered at all is derived from the plot width rather than measured**, so a bar too narrow to hold text does not put 31 characters in a 0×16px box.

**`lbl-cut` was a class name with no rule, in either codebase.** The truncate branch had always been a no-op wearing a name — and it works, because `.bar .bl` is already `overflow:hidden` with an ellipsis. The branch stays, because the *order* is the decision (outside, then truncated, then hidden) and a bar wide enough for a clipped label must not fall through to `nolabel`.

**Three ports finished.** The mockup's shared-prefix **stemming** is back — five bars reading "COD Point Rush Week 1".."Week 5" become "Week 1".."Week 5" with the full name on the tooltip and a dotted left edge saying the name was shortened rather than mis-entered. It is computed from the titles, never from rendered width, which is precisely why it was safe to port when its sibling pass was not: nothing it changes feeds back into the decision, and a test asserts it is idempotent on its own output. The Track's **zoom hint** now renders — `.zhint` and its `kbd` had been styled for a line nothing emitted, so the only way to discover the Track's own zoom was to guess it. And the deadline editor's row **emits its controls in the order its own grid was written for**: both stylesheets say `84px 104px` with `justify-self:start` on the switch, the markup emitted them reversed, and every row stopped 45px short of its own right edge. Nothing was wrong with the CSS.

**A Repairs check that reports zero, and means it.** COMPANION §5.2's most-cited finding — a calendar banner still pointing at a signed `media.discordapp.net` link, which 404s once its own deadline passes — is now one of Season's checks. Against the live document it finds **nothing**, because both databases were re-hosted, and that is the point: a panel that only shows problems cannot tell you what it is watching.

**Vocabulary.** The manifest's remove column said `STAGE DELETION`. `Delete` is the retired word — `Remove` for reversible, `Purge` for one-way — and `manifest.js` already defaulted correctly while Season overrode it.

**Three things this pass got wrong about itself, all the same way.** An absence read off a state that was never reached: Repairs' zero-state was filed as missing (it is built, and all three checks simply happened to be non-zero in the fixture), the banner rows' rhythm was filed as a footnote defect (it matches the mockup exactly), and eleven "mockup-only" classes turned out to have emitters behind states nobody had opened. **The instrument that was right every time was relational** — comparing two things that should agree — and both real geometry defects came from a pair disagreeing.

**And the mockup's Board was retired three days before the mockup was drawn.** `season.html` and COMPANION §5.2 describe content-state columns; the portal renders the changeset pipeline, which is `2026-08-20-web-admin-portal-design.md` §F3. A precedence rule reading *"the newer artifact wins"* inverts here — the mockup never adopted its own project's decision — and following it mechanically would have rebuilt a screen that had been deliberately replaced. Recorded as COMPANION §16.34, §16.35 and §16.36, because a divergence the design package does not carry is a defect in the package.

**Twenty-one Season states are registered and walk clean at 1282×888**, and registering them found three more defects: the states driver's `type` step read a shape none of its siblings use, so it typed nothing into nothing and only the `expect` guard reported it; a step whose effect mounts the next step's target needed a settle it could not ask for; and the offline banner is reached by `?fail=offline` and not by the `?offline=` parameter that `async.js`'s own header and this plan's flag list both named — so a state registered under it would have walked the default view and passed.

**Finally, the dev portal was serving five-hour-old JavaScript while `curl` against the same origin returned the new bytes.** `portal/server.js` sent no `Cache-Control` at all, which is not neutral — a browser then caches heuristically off the file's age. It now sends `no-cache, must-revalidate` for the document and everything it executes. ⚠️ Cloudflare still overrides that to `max-age=14400` on the dev hostname; until a Cache Rule says otherwise, verify a portal change against `http://localhost:8787` rather than the tunnel.

### 2026-08-28 18:5x EDT — the page and the mockup get subtracted, and three of the differences were declarations that never applied

Part 1 of the portal conformance pass, second attempt. The first one closed Season on four green gates without anyone opening the page, and Harkirat reopened it with two screenshots. **What was missing was not a check but a KIND of check**: every instrument in this repo enumerates elements — does this class have a rule, does this rule have an element, do these states walk — and a page with all the right elements in the wrong arrangement passes every one of them. `scripts/portalDiff.mjs` renders the mockup and the real portal at the same viewport and subtracts them, so the work list is produced before anyone has an opinion about which elements are worth counting.

**Three of the differences it found were CSS declarations that had never applied to anything.** `.mh-add` has carried `grid-column`, `grid-row` and `justify-self:end` since the mockup, and `Masthead` rendered it inside `.mh-id` — not a grid item, so all three were inert and the ADD row right-aligned to the wrong element: measured on Season at 1282, it ended at **x=995 while the export line directly beneath it ended at x=1260**. Two right-aligned rows, one above the other, 265px apart. `.now::after{content:attr(data-now)}` has been in the stylesheet just as long and **nothing ever set `data-now`**, so COMPANION's *"one thin line and a chip"* has never once drawn its chip. And `.dfl` carried no casing rule, so the same deadline read `BATTLE PASS` in the masthead and `battle pass` on the Track's rail, 600px apart on one screen. Armory had the ADD-row defect identically and was fixed by the same change; all seven mastheads were rendered afterwards to prove it, and only Season's geometry fixture moved.

**The tool was measuring its own setup.** `mintSession` took `AdminUser.findOne({})`, which in the dev database is a scoped test admin holding three realms of six — so the rail rendered SEASON / BROADCAST / REVIEW against the mockup's six and **three of the first run's eleven regions were the diff reporting its own session**. It mints for the hardcoded owner now.

**`--view` refuses rather than attempts, because its failure mode is flattering.** Season's Board and Repairs live behind tabs; a click that misses on one side diffs the default view against itself and prints a small, tidy region list that reads like conformance. So each side records what `main` says before and after the click and the run is refused unless both actually moved — proved both ways, `--view Nonsense` exits 1 and `--view Board` lands with the breadcrumb reading *Season Board* on both sides. Board turned out to need no work at all: COMPANION describes content-state columns, and the portal's changeset pipeline is the supersession recorded in the web-admin-portal design spec §F3.

**`--viewport` exists because the plan's own out-of-scope line could not narrow his instruction.** Part 0 named *"1280×880 and 375×812"*; the execution plan said mobile was out of scope, and that plan was written here, not by him. Both stylesheets carry real `max-width:768px` rules, so the narrow layout is designed on both sides — **7.3% differ in 12 regions**, and what differs is ordering, not degradation.

🔴 **One fix was wrong on its first attempt, and the error is worth more than the fix.** `.srec-nudge` inside the season record and `.nodraft` 60px below it both announced that no next season was staged, so the nudge was deleted as a duplicate. They were not the same fact: the nudge fired only at **seven days or fewer**, so removing it would have deleted the page's only late warning while looking like tidying. The urgency now rides on `.nodraft`, which is the line that carries the title field and the button.

Also here: the dev portal stops being cached for four hours at the edge — the zone had no `http_request_cache_settings` entrypoint at all, so `.js` and `.css` through the tunnel took Cloudflare's default over the origin's own `no-cache`, and a rebuilt portal served a five-hour-old module graph while `curl` against the same origin returned the new bytes. Verified with a falsifier rather than a green reading: the same zone at a host the rule does not match still returns `MISS` then `EXPIRED` at `max-age=14400`.

**Season stays ◐, and the reason is the point of this entry.** Five differences remain open with evidence — the Track's Events and Playlists auto-collapsing 20 of 39 items, the overview scrubber's mark weight, Repairs implementing three of COMPANION §5.2's six checks, four export formats against five, and the window range's placement. The difference ledger is `local/difference-ledger-season.md` (gitignored — state the path). A row that says closed while a difference stands is what produced this second attempt.

### 2026-08-28 21:1x EDT — the two pages are made to produce the same pixels, and Broadcast reaches 0.3%

### 2026-08-31 15:0x EDT — a compliance hook was rebuilt three times in one afternoon, and each version was falsified by measurement rather than by argument

**V1 fired on nearly every turn, and hardest on the compliant ones.** `turn-shape-guard.sh` shipped that morning to warn about narration and one-at-a-time work. Its narration test asked whether a text block sat before the first tool call in a message, with `$firstTool` defaulting to `999` when a message had none — so every text-only message scored as narration. This is a Stop hook, and the last message of a well-formed turn is exactly the **one structured summary the working contract demands**. It also fired on a plain prose answer, on a turn correctly blocked awaiting push approval, and on the framing before an `AskUserQuestion`. Three shapes the contract requires. Its suite reported 8/8 throughout.

**V2 was mine, and was worse — it matched 0 of 13,922 real messages.** Requiring the prose to sit before a tool call *in the same message* describes a shape this transcript format cannot produce: text and tool calls are always separate assistant messages. A 140-character floor was added on the theory that real narration is long. **The suite went 21/21 on synthetic fixtures while the rule was dead.**

**Then the length theory was inverted, and then falsified outright.** The first correction was that narration is *short* — "Found it." is nine characters, and the measured histogram peaks at 50–100 while the floor sat at 140. Harkirat falsified that too, with a screenshot of a real session: page-long structured blocks, tables included, sitting between tool calls all morning. Measured across **3,775 real instances: 13 to 7,869 characters, median 128, mass in every band.** 🔴 **Length is not the discriminator in either direction. Position is** — a text-only message with more tool calls after it is mid-turn commentary, whatever it says and however long. The rule is now purely positional, with no regex, no length bound and no tunable constant, and only the two carve-outs Harkirat states himself: a note while waiting on a long background task, and the framing immediately before a popup.

🔴 **And one binary trigger was still wrong, because narration is situation-dependent.** Position detects a candidate; it cannot judge one. A single substantive checkpoint halfway through a long autonomous run is legitimate — the same block repeated after every tool call is running commentary, and the earlier versions treated them identically, which is what made the hook read as friction rather than help. Each mid-turn block is now classified on four independent signals: **HEDGE** (opens by pre-registering intent — delete it, there is nothing to move), **ACK** (a contentless reaction), **DUPLICATE** (its distinctive words already appear in the turn's own final summary, so the reader pays twice), and **CADENCE** (prose keeping pace 1:1 with the work). A block that is none of these stays silent.

🔴 **The test underneath all four is redundancy and importance, and only the session can apply it** — Harkirat's framing: *is this important enough to say right now, or can it wait for the checkpoint summary, and will it be repeated there anyway?* DUPLICATE approximates that mechanically by word overlap with the final message; the warning also asks the question outright, because a guard that reports only a count teaches silence, and the goal is compliance.

🔴 **The deeper error was optimising for RARITY when the target is TRUTH.** Every threshold was being tuned to make the hook fire less: at run ≥3 it fired on 71.5% of 615 real turns, at ≥8 on 51.4%, at ≥20 on 30.1% — no cut point existed, and moving 2→3 changed 76.6% to 71.5%, which is nothing. "A good alert is a rare alert" comes from monitoring, where alerts compete for a human's scarce attention. **The reader here is Claude, so alert fatigue is not the governing constraint and the rate IS the finding**: narration occurs in 76.6% of turns at a mean of 6.1 per turn against a contract of zero.

**And the clauses were split across three events, because a Stop hook is a post-mortem that cannot change the turn it measures.** Asking which event each clause wants is the question the first two versions never asked. `batch-edit-guard.sh` is **PreToolUse**: it fires at the second edit to a file already edited this turn, while the rest can still be collapsed into one heredoc, and it has **no escape hatch** — unlike a read-chain, a second edit to a known file is never waiting on the first one's output, and any non-edit call resets the map by construction so edit → test → fix-what-the-test-found does not fire. `audit-think-gate.sh` is **UserPromptSubmit**, covering the one contract clause carrying the word *mandatorily*: sequential thinking on an audit or review. `turn-shape-guard.sh` keeps only what is genuinely retrospective.

⚠️ **The suites gained the case class whose absence let two broken versions ship: a replay against real transcripts**, asserting the rule fires on some turns and is silent on others. A predicate that hits 0% or 100% of real turns is broken whatever the hand-written cases say — and neither V1 nor V2 could have failed a hand-written case. On the shipped version the replay reports **38 of 40 real turns firing**, which is not a tuning failure but the measurement of how much narration these sessions actually contain.

A test nobody runs is worse than no test, because it produces a documented belief that the behaviour is covered."* It happened again anyway, which is the argument for the fix being verified rather than asserted: the three gates were put in the chain and then **proven by planting a wrong permission-token count in `COMPANION.md` and watching `npm test` go red**, then restoring it and watching it go green — not by reading `package.json`.

**The cache-buster was the last admitted-unenforced step.** COMPANION §15.8 said so in as many words — the `?v=` stamp is *"bumped by hand when an asset changes"* — while a stale asset had already produced three false "verified" claims in that package's history and thirty-five references had just been bumped by hand with nothing checking. ## Pre-Release v3.68.0 — 2026-08-26 19:36 EDT (#175) — the draw calculator becomes one live panel

The old `/draw calculator` was a setup form: pick a draw, pick a goal, open a modal, type two numbers, submit, press Calculate — five interactions before a single figure appeared, and Harkirat called it "terrible, lacks intuitive, lacks design/style, and is not user friendly." It is rebuilt from the ground up.

**One always-live panel, not two stages.** Every figure is a pure function of the state carried in the button/select `customId`, so recomputing on every click costs a few thousand integer operations against a Discord round trip — there was never a reason for a separate "Calculate" step. `pullsDone` and the target pull are now selects, enumerated from the draw's real pull count, so an out-of-range value can no longer be typed in the first place; only genuinely free-form amounts (a CP balance, a CP budget) still open a one-field modal. A real landing state was added — the command used to open straight into a random draw with no explanation of what the dropdowns or buttons were for.

**Rebuilt a second time against Harkirat's own mockup.** Three earlier passes each guessed at "better structure" from first principles and were each rejected on his live screenshots. He then exported a real Components V2 message he'd built himself, and the COST BREAKDOWN block was rebuilt to match it directly — reusing `/draw prices`' own `buildDrawEntries()` for the top summary so the two commands render the same draw identically instead of two similar-but-different copies, and adding progressive disclosure ("Show Breakdown" / "Simplify") so the collapsed view isn't a wall of numbers.

**Three rounds of live mobile polish followed**, each from a screenshot on the running dev bot: code-spans are now reserved for the figures a player actually acts on (total price, total CP, what's left over) rather than boxing every number, since a long or multi-part value wraps mid-box on a narrow phone; the blockquote-prefixed label marker was replaced with a plain bullet after it rendered as an unwanted vertical bar down the page; and the region label moved off the `## COST BREAKDOWN` heading onto its own caption line after it started wrapping into the title.

The two commands are cross-linked (`/draw calculator` ↔ `/draw prices`, zero new handler code either way, both routing through each command's own existing custom_id scheme), and three new emoji assets were added (`calculator`, `mythicCard`, `mythicCoin`) — verified against the dev application only, since prod credentials aren't available from this worktree.

Not yet click-tested live end-to-end on the dev bot in a formal pass (it was exercised heavily via the live screenshot-feedback loop above); filed in `docs/db-deferred-list.md`'s 🔔 Reminders with the specific sequence still owed.

## Pre-Release v3.67.0 — 2026-08-23 14:08 EDT (#174 · `4a7971e`) — five tracker entries that described work already done

Its `needs-design` flag was discharged by the implementation deciding the design question was the wrong one.

🔑 **And a push went out that nobody had authorized.** `okay merge` was said about one PR; that approval was consumed by that merge, and a branch created twenty minutes later reached `origin` twice on the strength of it. **The rule was loaded in context from two places at the time** — CLAUDE.md and `MEMORY.md`'s index — so this was never a knowledge gap. Measured that day: 28 hooks, and **every enforcement one is about correctness**, none about authorization. `.claude/hooks/push-approval-gate.sh` now demands `Approved by / to / when` at the moment of any real `git push`, naming the five rationalisations that actually fired. It does not deny — a gate that blocks would stop a push approved in the same breath — and it stays silent on `--dry-run` and `--delete`, since gating the undo would make cleanup harder than the mistake.

**The shared shape is worth naming.** Every stale entry asserted an *absence* — "no way to", "never lets you", "has no". That is the one kind of item the code can silently invalidate, because filling the gap leaves the list untouched. Nothing checks for it, so re-read an absence claim against the code before working it.

## Pre-Release v3.66.0 — 2026-08-23 13:05 EDT (#173) — the change panel covers every entity, and a permission check that compared against nothing

Phase 2 of the analytics work, and three of its own premises turned out to be false — which is most of what this release is. ⚠️ **This and v3.65.0-pre below ship in the SAME pull request** — phase 1 was never separately merged, so both entries cite `#173`. They stay two entries because they are two versions of the code and two distinct bodies of work, not because they were two merges.

🔴 **A permission gate was comparing against a string no grant can hold.** `core/changeset.js`'s `pageForOp()` fell back to an op's own namespace for the six ops that have no `/manage` action by design, and that namespace is not the permission vocabulary. Four patch-note ops recorded **`patchnote`** (singular) — so `hasManagePageAccess(userId, 'patchnote')` could never match `manage.patchnotes`, and every scoped admin was silently denied on those rows. `season.restoreDraft` was wrong in **both** directions: it recorded `season` while reversing a *draft* discard, denying `manage.seasondraft` admins their own page and letting `manage.season`-only admins reach draft state. Ops now declare `page:` beside `action:`, registration throws if the two disagree, and a subset assertion that **failed before this change** guards it permanently. `scripts/fixChangeLogPageKeys.js` repairs existing rows.

🔴 **A rule the last release recorded as "adopted verbatim" was applied to one branch out of two.** The stacked before/after notation — one value per line, each led by its own glyph — reached the *list* diff and never reached the *scalar* diff, which kept shipping the inline `A → B` the rule exists to forbid. On a 32-column phone that is the difference between reading `Drop` vs `Draw` and guessing. Fixed, with a test that reads the source and fails on an arrow. **A design spec cannot be validated by reading it — including the spec that says so.**

**Loadouts and calendar events now draw themselves.** `utils/loadoutRender.js` splits into a content half and its chrome, so a build renders in the panel without dragging in pagination buttons whose ids resolve against a query only `/gunsmiths` has made. `/calendar` exports the entry line it already uses. Neither is a copy: a copied renderer drifts, and a panel that quietly stops matching the real card is worse than one that never tried.

**"Is this live to players?" — asked, and answered honestly.** The planned line assumed a draw's date decides whether players see it. It does not: `/draws` lists every draw in the season document with no filter of any kind, so the date is a label it prints. The panel says that instead. `/calendar` genuinely does hide ended entries, and takes its answer from the same `isEventEnded()` the command uses rather than a second date rule that would drift.

**The audit pass found a defect in its own fix.** `registerEntity()`'s new conflict check originally ran *after* the registry writes, so a rejected op stayed resolvable and its action stayed claimed. `assert.throws(..., /message/)` passed against exactly that — asserting an error fires proves nothing about what the failure left behind. The check now runs before any mutation, and the test asserts the rejection is clean rather than merely loud.

**One crash that had been waiting for a partial record.** `buildImageUrl()` calls `.startsWith()` on `imageKey`; every stored build has one, so `/gunsmiths` never hit it — but a reconstructed before-state carries only the fields an edit touched. The panel's own try/catch would have swallowed it and fallen back silently, which is a budget guard firing for the wrong reason.

## Pre-Release v3.65.0 — 2026-08-23 11:34 EDT (#173) — `/bot analytics` becomes five glances, and the change log becomes readable

The plan and spec filed in v3.64.0, built — and then substantially rebuilt, five times, against a real Discord client on desktop and on a phone. The rebuild is the bigger half of this release and most of it came from looking at the rendered thing rather than re-reading the design.

**The five pages.** Discord is a glance now; the portal carries the depth. Every page drops its pager, filters and Export button for one Link button into the matching portal view — the portal was confirmed to already carry all of it, including revert, before anything was cut, so nothing here is a removal. **Health** states a verdict then an aligned vitals block. **Alerts** keeps the severity ledger, cut to the 3 most recent. **Changes** is a ledger of the 3 most recent edits. **Usage** draws proportional bars against the leading command. **Timing** states every number against what actually constrains it.

🔴 **Timing was asserting a production fault that did not exist.** It measured total duration against Discord's 3,000 ms limit — but that limit is the deadline to *acknowledge* an interaction; after a defer the window is fifteen minutes. A heavy image command working exactly as designed rendered as `🔴 /colors -204% headroom`. Headroom now applies to the ack alone; duration gets a felt-speed band on Nielsen's published thresholds.

🔴 **And nobody could read it anyway.** `p50`, `p95` and "headroom" all failed on the page's only reader. They are "usually", "slowest 1 in 20", and the rule plus what it consumes — translations chosen to stay true, not merely simpler.

🔴 **Revert used to fire blind.** A row read "Added new draw" and offered a button that immediately undid it. Tapping now opens a detail panel that renders **the actual record, using the record's own renderer** — a draw draws itself exactly as `/draws` shows it — with a real before/after for edits, reconstructed from the inverse's stored previous values. Revert lives in there behind a red button, beside an Edit that dispatches through the existing action registry. Crucially it also names **any later change that touched the same record**, because reverting writes old values back over whatever came after it.

**Mobile changed several verdicts.** ANSI colour is stripped silently on iOS, so colour is decoration and never meaning — severity leads with a glyph instead. The VM-peaks block ran 46 columns and wrapped into four ragged lines; the real budget measures near 32, not the 40 the spec estimated, and that spec had cited the wrapping function itself as its own precedent.

**Two defects the panel found in other people's code.** `pageForOp()` emits `patchnote` (singular) as well as `patchnotes` for four ops with no registered action — a key no scope list contains, which the revert permission gate is being called with. Filed, not patched; the owner is the action registry. And `docs-audit`'s `superseded_by` existence check had never once executed, because nothing in the repo used the field; it threw a `ReferenceError` on first use while its own self-test passed the entire time, because a crashed check reports under the same id as a real finding. Both the check and the self-test harness are fixed — a proof is now rejected if the check only "reported" by crashing.

Change ids are `#284` now rather than `Aug22-28`, which read as a second, contradicting date beside the real timestamp. Old ids still resolve.

## Pre-Release v3.64.0 — 2026-08-23 00:09 EDT (#172) — a copy-pasteable retry for every failed `/manage` submit, loadout images by URL, and a bulk format that finally has a principle

Four items off the deferred list, one deferred by name, and one turned into a spec instead of code.

**Every failed `/manage` submit now hands you your work back.** A rejected add, edit, or bulk paste replies with what you entered — reconstructed in that entity's own bulk format, so it pastes back into either the field it came from or that entity's Bulk Add — plus a **Try Again** button that reopens the same form already refilled. 14 modals, 12 failure branches across draws, calendar and loadouts. The button rather than a modal is Discord's rule, not a preference: a modal submit cannot be answered with another modal. The snippet and the button expire differently on purpose — the button lasts 10 minutes, the text doesn't expire at all — which is why both were worth having.

**Loadout images can be a URL now.** The Cloudinary Image Key field on Add and Edit takes either a Public ID or a pasted image link, told apart by the URL scheme, so it needed no sixth field in a modal that was already at Discord's hard five-field cap. On Edit the upload lands on the build's *existing* key, so swapping a picture never breaks anything pointing at it. If Cloudinary is unreachable the raw URL is saved instead of the save failing — already a supported state, and the same fallback draw thumbnails have always had.

**The loadout bulk format was rewritten**, and the complaint behind it turned out to be exactly right. Asked why some things were on one line and others on their own, the honest answer was that there was no principle to state. There is one now — identity on the first line, every optional field on its own labelled line, everything else an attachment — and the old seven-segment pipe line is rejected outright rather than half-parsed, at Harkirat's call.

🔴 **Reading that format for the rewrite turned up a real bug.** The parser *required* a Mode field that the save path then threw away and replaced with whichever page you were on. Confirmed live before anything changed: a block typed `DMZ`, pasted into the MP page, parsed with zero errors and saved as MP — and since Export emitted Mode too, exporting DMZ builds and pasting them on the MP page silently reassigned every one of them. Mode is gone from the format; the page has always been what decided it.

**`/bot analytics` got a design spec and an 8-task plan rather than a rebuild.** The report that Alerts and Changes "show the exact same info" was checked first, because a data bug would have been a one-line fix — they read different collections entirely. What is real is that all five pages are one skeleton differing only in accent colour, so on a quiet bot they collapse into the same near-empty panel. Mid-drafting the whole thing was reframed: the web portal now carries in-depth analytics, so Discord becomes a glance — one question, one screenful, with pagers and filters and exports moving to the portal. The portal was checked to actually carry all of it, including revert, before the spec relied on that.

New emoji for `/manage`'s Announcement page, `/bot access` and `/help`'s Bot Admin category, and `/invite`'s Share Link button. DMZ Loadouts stays deliberately open — asked about and deferred by name, with the real gameplay differences recorded for when it comes back. 28 new tests; an audit pass before merge found one more defect (a stray trailing pipe being diagnosed as the retired format) and fixed it.

**Four more real, previously-shipped bugs found integrating this — the most severe of which crashed the whole portal server.** `core/changeset.js`'s `previewSet()` never awaited its ops' `preview()` calls: loadouts' and announcements' edit/delete previews are `async`, so an unawaited rejection became an unhandled promise rejection that killed the entire Node process on a single malformed op. Reproduced live twice pre-fix; the identical request now logs a caught error and the server keeps serving everything after it. Also fixed: `season.js` ESM-imported from `season.logic.js`, a classic-script-loaded file with no `export` statement — throws in every real browser, undetected until this pass because no prior verification had actually loaded Season as real ESM; a local `const window` in `season.js` shadowed the real browser global, breaking Export Selection's `window.open()` call; and `core/ops/calendar.js`'s `validateEvent` reads the start date from `payload.startDate` while the stored field is `date` — the same field-name-mismatch class already found once for draws, found again for calendar.

## Pre-Release v3.59.0 — 2026-08-21 19:05 EDT (#168) — the remaining 5 entities wired onto the operation core, and a branch-wide review that found the core's own sharp edges

Plan 2 of the portal operation-core refactor: `calendar`/`loadouts`/`patchnotes`/`season`/`announcements` now all route their DB mutations through `core/changeset.js`'s `commitSet`, matching the pattern plan 1 already established for `draws` — every mutation validates as a batch, applies inside one real Mongo transaction, and records a `ChangeLog` row carrying a real `inverse`. The old in-memory Undo store (`handlers/manage/shared.js`'s `registerUndo`/`manageUndoStore`) is retired entirely; every entity's revert now lives permanently on `/bot analytics`' Changes page (`core/revert.js`), backed by Mongo instead of a same-session-only Map that vanished on restart.

**A 13-agent code review across the whole branch (both plan 1 and plan 2's ranges) found 10 real bugs, all fixed.** The two most severe were both in the operation core itself, not in any one entity: `commitSet` validated its `ops` array *before* flattening it, so any op whose `invert()` returns an ARRAY (`draw.bulkDelete`/`draw.purge`, and the newly-added `loadout.bulkAdd`/`bulkReplace`) made clicking Revert fail unconditionally with "unknown op type undefined" — the exact shape `core/revert.js`'s `revertChange` always produces; and `pageForOp` always took `action[0]` of a multi-page-registered op, permanently mislabeling every DMZ loadout mutation's `ChangeLog` row as `loadouts_mp`, which would have both broken analytics' page filter for DMZ and let a `loadouts_mp`-scoped admin revert a DMZ change they hold no grant for (or blocked a `loadouts_dmz`-scoped admin from reverting their own). Also fixed: `draw.bulkAdd` computed its new ids via a post-resort tail-slice, which silently grabs the wrong ids — and therefore deletes the wrong draws on revert — whenever a newly-added draw's date sorts earlier than an existing one; `loadout.bulkAdd`/`bulkReplace`'s `invert()` only deleted newly-created docs, leaving any build the same paste overwrote in place permanently un-revertable; a transaction-retry accumulator bug where `changeIds`/`results` could double-count across a MongoDB `TransientTransactionError` retry; `editLoadout` hanging an interaction forever on a stale id (deferred, never followed up); two unawaited replies in `handlers/bot.js`'s revert branch, against the documented crash-net convention; `previewSet` crashing on any bulk op; a read-side gap where the already-settable `Announcement.startsAt` was never checked; and a bare `docs:audit` npm script silently dropped by an earlier merge-conflict resolution, breaking CI's audit step for 9+ commits without anyone noticing.

**7 lower-severity findings from the same review were fixed in a follow-up pass**, not left deferred: `core/mongo/positional.js` gained a shared `resortByDate` (hoisted out of a byte-identical `draws.js`/`calendar.js` duplicate, now returning the sorted array so both entities' `bulkAdd` drop a redundant third fetch); `core/ops/patchnotes.js`'s Cloudinary uploads now run via `Promise.all` (verified safe against the transaction session first); `handlers/manage/patchnotes.js`'s `reloadEntry()` post-commit-read bandaid is gone, replaced by `title`/`imageCount` surfaced directly on the op's own `applied`, matching how the other 4 entities solved the same problem; a handful of dead exports and duplicated logic were cleaned up, including a shared `extractCommitError(result)` helper replacing 31 copies of the same error-extraction expression across the 6 entity handlers.

Full `npm test` green throughout; `npm run check`/`docs:audit`/`docs:reflow`/`docs:reflow-comments` all clean.

## Pre-Release v3.58.0 — 2026-08-21 12:30 EDT (#167 · `ccca561`) — parallelized check/hooks/audit-self-test, with a session-scoped test cache

Ported speed wins from the gif-background-remover skill's own harness work: `node --check` runs `-P 8` (44.6s → 1.7–5.0s); `.claude/hooks/run-all-tests.sh` replaces a hand-rolled busy-poll scheduler with `xargs -P` (53.4s → 16–21s); `scripts/docs-audit.test.mjs`'s 71 checks are now sharded across N node subprocesses (~110–115s → ~40–55s), guarded by a cross-shard total-slot-count invariant so a desynced or malformed shard assignment fails loudly instead of reporting a false pass.

New `scripts/testCache.mjs` is a session-scoped cache (gitignored `local/.test-cache/`): hashes actual input bytes plus the wrapped command, skips re-running only on an exact match to a prior *pass*, never caches a failure, and treats `CI=true` as an automatic bypass so CI's own deliberate second `docs:audit:test` invocation still re-runs for real rather than replaying a cache hit within the same job. Wraps `docs:audit:test` and `test:hooks`; full `npm test` drops from ~92s cold to ~28–31s warm.

**Two full rounds of parallel code review (8 finder angles each), all findings fixed, caught real defects — not cosmetic ones.** Round 1 (10 findings): `HOOK_TEST_JOBS=0` deadlocked the hook suite forever; the cache's own self-test leaked real cache files into the repo (`local/.test-cache/` isolation was broken by a `cwd` override that had no effect on where `testCache.mjs` actually resolves its cache directory, since that's derived from the script's own file location); a cache entry was keyed on input-file hash alone, never the wrapped command, so changing `package.json`'s command without touching the hashed files would have served a stale pass for code that was never executed; a spawn failure was silently downgraded to a bare exit code with no diagnostic text. Round 2 (7 findings, on the docs-audit sharding specifically): the single most severe defect this branch produced — a malformed `DOCS_AUDIT_TEST_SHARD` value made every check silently skip while `docs-audit.test.mjs` still printed `✅ all 0 checks proven capable of failing`, a self-congratulating false pass in the file whose entire job is catching exactly that failure mode. Fixed with a parse-time validation that refuses to run rather than silently skip, plus a cross-shard invariant (every shard must agree on the total check-slot count, and executed checks summed across shards must equal it) that structurally can't be bypassed the way the unguarded version was.

**A third bug, caught by direct verification rather than either review round:** the fix for the total-slot-count invariant itself had a `||` short-circuit (`SHARD_N <= 1 || __idx++ % SHARD_N === SHARD_I`) that skipped the counter increment entirely on the default unsharded path — which would have produced a false-positive "some checks silently never ran" failure the first time anyone ran `DOCS_AUDIT_TEST_JOBS=1`. Found by actually running that exact configuration and reading the number, not by reasoning about the code. Fixed and re-verified under that configuration, plus a real failure-injection re-check (a deliberately broken check correctly caught, exactly one failure reported, byte-identical file restoration afterward) on the final code.

## Pre-Release v3.57.0 — 2026-08-20 22:54 EDT (#166 · `ecb7958`) — the portal's ship-after-v3.0.0 gate, reversed

⚠️ **A note on this entry's own timestamp.** Its first draft was stamped `23:00 EDT` while the clock read `22:54` — estimated, not read. `.claude/hooks/timestamp-check.sh` caught it on the DEVLOG write and denied the tool call, but the same fabricated stamp had already reached the spec, the ROADMAP and this file in an earlier commit. All three are corrected to `22:54`. Recorded rather than quietly fixed, because the 2026-08-02 incident this hook exists for produced thirty well-formed fabricated stamps and the only thing wrong with any of them was that nobody had looked at a clock.

## Pre-Release v3.56.0 — 2026-08-20 22:10 EDT (#165) — the changelog's PR citation, gated

Nothing changed in the bot. v3.55.0 shipped citing a literal `(#PR)`; this fills it to `(#164)`, backfills v3.54.0's squash hash `9cb560a`, and adds a **`changelog-pr-cite`** ERROR check to `scripts/docs-audit.mjs` so the class cannot recur. **The placeholder is structural rather than careless**, which is why a check rather than more care: the pre-merge changelog entry is composed *on the branch*, where the PR number does not yet exist. Every audit check passed on it — version coverage, hash chain, record structure — because none of them read whether a citation is a *number*. The check is deliberately narrow, flagging placeholder shapes only (`(#PR)`, `(#XXX)`, `(#TBD)`) and never a missing citation, which has legitimate historical instances in that file. It scans headings only, so a body paragraph discussing the placeholder does not trip it — verified by appending one and confirming the audit stayed green.

**The check failed twice before it worked, and both failures were silent.** It first returned a `problems` key: every other check in that file returns **`findings`**, the runner reads only that, so it **passed green while doing nothing** — vacuous in exactly the case it existed for. It then returned bare strings, which the renderer prints as `undefined` while still failing the run. Neither was visible from reading it; both were caught by injecting `(#PR)` and watching the exit code. Both causes are now comments at the return site, and a `proves()` case pins the behaviour. **The structural remedy is ordering, not diligence** — open the PR first, then write the entry with the real number — and that is what this release did.

## Pre-Release v3.55.0 — 2026-08-20 20:15 EDT (#164) — the web admin portal, designed: spec, three plans, and 28 defects a context-free reader found in them

Nothing changed in the bot. A design-only pass producing `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-20-web-admin-portal-design.md` and three dependency-ordered plans for **`portal.dioreo.app`** — a browser admin console, Discord-OAuth-gated, that does everything `/manage` does plus scheduling, previewing, diffing and search-then-tick bulk editing that a Discord modal physically cannot host. `/manage` stays live and its behaviour unchanged. Ships after v3.0.0. **This supersedes the `[P2 · L]` "real search + multi-select flow" roadmap item** — Harkirat changed his mind on the implementation, not the goal, so that item is struck in place in both trackers rather than deleted, and `.claude/rules/manage-panel.md`'s own "Build the real version next, not a silent gap" instruction was struck too: that file auto-loads on any `commands/manage.js` edit and would otherwise have read as a live to-do.

The design is an **operation algebra** — every mutation becomes a value `{ type, target, payload }` with four verbs (`validate`/`preview`/`apply`/`invert`) that both Discord and the web drive, which also gives `/manage` durable undo surviving a restart, replacing an in-memory closure Map. A **three-tier hybrid model** derived from reversibility rather than assigned per button, where tier 3 will not commit until what it destroys has been exported — nearly free, because `utils/adminParser.js`'s formatters already round-trip through its own parsers. **Element-identity concurrency**, forced by reading the schema: `SeasonalData` is one global document, so ordinary `__v` locking would fire false conflicts on every pair of unrelated edits while a plain `.save()` silently reverts the other one. And a **two-layer information architecture** across five realms, with shape carrying state and colour carrying topic — Harkirat's correction, and the better rule, because shape survives greyscale and colourblindness.

**All six premises the design rests on were measured rather than assumed**, and one nearly derailed it for a reason unrelated to the design: transactions work on the M0 cluster (probed in a throwaway database, 0 of 2 after a rollback, 2 of 2 after a commit), element-identity concurrency behaves exactly as specified including rejecting a stale prior-value assertion, storage is at 0.15% of 512 MB, the VM has 390 MB available with the bot at 131 MB — not the ~600 MB the spec had derived from month-old figures — `buildLoadoutCard()` imports zero discord.js and yields production emoji ids without a client, and `cloudflared` is not installed. The near-miss: the transaction probe was pinned to `.env.dev` by a guard written to keep it safe, and that database is a **standalone**, so it would have failed and been read as "M0 does not support transactions".

**A reader-test agent with no session context found 28 defects that three falsification passes had missed**, and every one spot-checked was confirmed. Four were fatal — a circular `require` that made the first file fail on load with a TypeError, a conservation test mathematically incapable of passing over a 1:1 map holding ten actions and seven ops, three of seven inverses destroyed by re-validation so undo silently restored nothing, and `recordChange` returning `undefined` with no session so audit rows escaped the transaction. One was a privilege escalation: the Revert control trusted the `bot_` router prefix, which proves *some* `/bot` access rather than page scope. Three were false claims about existing code, each a single grep away — `patchConsole()` takes no parameters, `scripts/buildLegalPages.js` has no `module.exports`, `handlers/router.js` never imports `ALLOWED_ADMIN_ID`. **The generalizable lesson is recorded in the spec's audit log: the earlier passes audited the design and never ran the plan's own code as code.**

Repairing those exposed a second bug, in this repo's own tooling. An orphaned fence left by one of the fixes gave a plan an odd fence count; `scripts/reflow-prose.mjs` pairs fences positionally, so a later opening fence was consumed as an earlier block's close and **nine code blocks after that point were reflowed as prose and collapsed onto single lines**, including an entire module implementation. `verify()` passed, because it compares fenced-block *content* and under a mispairing compared the same wrong blocks before and after — a vacuous check. The plan was restored from the last clean commit and all 22 fixes re-applied deterministically; `reflow-prose.mjs` now reports an odd fence count as its own problem before any content comparison, with two test cases including a falsifier for the guard itself, proven by disabling it and watching the suite go red.

## Pre-Release v3.53.0 — 2026-08-20 13:16 EDT (#162 · `a5f626b`) — Hotpatch v1: reload a pulled file into the running bot without a restart

Ships the design from `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-20-hotpatch-design.md`. `utils/hotpatch.js` computes a static require-graph closure for a set of changed files and classifies it `ALLOW` / `REFUSE_STATE` (live module state with no `__hotSwap` contract) / `REFUSE_STRUCTURAL` (`index.js`/`bot/`/`models/` in the closure, or an unresolved path) — the invariant is that a reload is sound iff its closure terminates at a late-bound boundary and every member is stateless or opts in. `handlers/router.js` now resolves its 15 handler modules at call time instead of capturing them once at require, which is what makes them hot-swappable and what keeps `router.js` itself a boundary rather than a closure member. `applyHotpatch` is verify-then-swap, all-or-nothing: a `node --check` syntax gate, a snapshot of `require.cache` and `client.commands`, the actual swap, shape validation (a changed Discord-facing command shape — new command, changed option or description — is refused, since the command list only updates via one REST `PUT` at boot), then either re-wire or roll back to the exact snapshot. Two fire surfaces: `/bot hotpatch` (owner-only, `pull`/`dry_run`/`file` options, a panel that either confirms what applied or refuses with a reason plus Full-restart/Cancel buttons) and `scripts/hotpatch.mjs` over a `SIGUSR2` signal to the running process, for the phone/no-Discord case. The baseline commit a hotpatch diffs against comes from `utils/logger.js`'s `currentCommit()` (now a getter over a hotpatch-updated `let`, via the new `noteHotpatch()`), never `git rev-parse HEAD` — Harkirat pulls separately and then hotpatches, so `HEAD` is already the new commit by the time a hotpatch runs, and diffing against it would silently no-op forever. Ships with zero `__hotSwap` declarations by design; nine files hold nearly all the blockable state and each opts in only when it actually blocks a wanted patch — see `.claude/rules/hotpatch.md`. Also fixes `.claude/hooks/self-check.sh`'s model-selection gate, found live during this branch's own completeness sweep: the gate's "already given, do not repeat it" short-circuit checked only the model-derivation shape, so stating that alone silently satisfied its own request for the `/rename` string too. Adds a second, deliberately stricter detector for the rename-string shape and requires both before going quiet.
