## Pre-Release v3.51.0 — 2026-08-19 14:03 EDT (#159 · `07b67e2`) — dioreo.app's /commands page becomes a command builder, and an accent stops being used as a text colour

The website's fourth page family: **`/commands`**, a reference for every public Dioreo command that reads the bot's own command builders at build time, so it cannot drift from what the bot actually registers. `scripts/lib/commandCatalog.js` calls `.toJSON()` on every module in `commands/` and files each leaf under the group `commands/help.js`'s own `CATEGORY_DEFS` puts it in — so the website and the in-Discord directory cannot disagree about how the bot is organised — and **throws, naming the command, if a public one has nowhere to go**. `scripts/lib/commandProse.js` supplies the one thing Discord cannot: why a person would want the command, gated both ways so prose without a command and a command without prose both fail the build. `scripts/lib/commandsPage.js` renders it. Accent is Signal Green 121°, the midpoint of the widest gap on the nav's hue wheel (citron 62° → teal 180°), and the nav restaged from six tabs to seven, ten inside `/changelog/`, both tiers measured in a browser rather than arithmetic'd from the old ones.

**The misalignment Harkirat reported was not a design problem, and the cause is worth writing down.** `.bar`, `.bar nav{margin-left:auto}` and `.page` — the site's entire chrome layout — were written out *verbatim* in `shell()`, `warmShell()` and `scripts/lib/chronicle.js`: three byte-identical copies and no shared constant. So a fourth family could be added carrying the bar **markup** and none of its **styling**, and every gate stayed green, because the build checks content, links, class collisions, contrast and coverage and **never whether a class resolves to a rule at all**. Measured on the shipped file: `public/commands.html` contained zero `.bar`, `.bar nav`, `.page` or `#prog` rules. Extracted as `CHROME.BAR_CSS` and `CHROME.PAGE_CSS` and collapsed all three copies; the other eight pages are unchanged apart from one emitted CSS comment that is now a JS comment (`terms.html` is 768 bytes lighter, `contributing.html` and `changelog/index.html` identical ignoring whitespace). The three markup deviations went with it: the bar's four controls now sit inside the `<nav>` that `margin-left:auto` targets, the content sits in `.page` instead of a private wrapper 40px narrower with no top padding for the fixed bar, and `pageFoot()` is the last child of `.page` rather than stretching to the full viewport.

**A phone could not reach the command list at all.** `.cx-fold{display:none}` sat *after* the media rule that shows it; both selectors are `(0,1,0)`, so source order decided and the base rule won at every width — the button was never visible anywhere. Combined with `setOpen()` deliberately collapsing the picker below 880px, a phone got a search box, no list, and no control to open one, on the page most likely to be read on a phone. Fixed by moving the base declaration above the media block and verified at a real 390px touch viewport: the button measures 39px, one click opens 340px of list and all 16 rows. Two coarse-pointer targets that measured 27px and 31px were raised past 32px in the same pass.

**The page is "the Receiver", and it took five rounds to get there.** The one before it — two zones, a dot column, a coloured panel — was chosen from renders and then failed on a phone, which is where this page is read. Measured at 375×812: the command index began 2.3 screenfuls down and was **855px tall**, one command's panel was **1282px**, and the command line — the artifact a reader came for — sat at **y=1339**, below everything. A layout whose whole premise is "both zones always on screen" had a mobile mode where neither was, and it degraded into exactly the single-scrolling-column shape that had already been rejected two rounds earlier. The page now has **one shape in both modes**: a rail of fourteen coloured command chips that wraps into grouped rows on a wide screen and scrolls horizontally on a narrow one, and a panel whose command line is sticky — under the rail on desktop, pinned to the bottom of the viewport on a phone. Opening a command on mobile fell from a **3010px** document to **1219px**, and the panel itself from 1282px to 660px, because a fifteen-item timezone list is now a 46px row you open rather than 348px you scroll past. The interaction is still `:target`, so it still needs no JavaScript, and **there is now a way back** — the rail's first chip and the Escape key. There was none: the only route to the landing state was the "Who sees it" link, which pointed at a guide inside the home panel, so following it silently discarded the command you were reading.

**The panel stopped describing the command and started building it.** Options were read-only pills and the one *required* option — the one that decides whether the command runs at all — was a bordered read-only block wearing a `REQUIRED` badge, which every convention on the web reads as *disabled*. The affordance was exactly inverted: the only control that mattered was the only one you could not touch. A required option is now a real control — a text input seeded with the sample when Discord takes free text, a pre-selected pill set when it takes a fixed list, and never both wrong ways round. **And a required option can no longer fall out of the copy line.** The client repaint built the line from the set of values the reader had picked; a free-text required option can never be in that set, so `/timestamp datetime sun 4:30pm` became `/timestamp timezone (UTC−04:00) Eastern` the instant anything optional was touched, and the page handed the reader a command Discord rejects. The line is now built from the command's *option list*, every option holds a permanent seat, an unfilled one draws as a visible gap, and Copy refuses with "Needs datetime" rather than copying something broken.

**An identity colour was being used as a text colour, and that was the worst thing on the page.** Each command's accent is picked for a Discord embed, and the page was bending it into readable text by walking its lightness until it measured 4.5:1. Patch Gold `#F2C230` came out `#7C5F08` in light theme — a 31-point lightness drop, which is brown — Neon Amber came out rust, and the raw hex sat in a dot forty pixels away, so the page showed two different colours for one command and called it recognition. Dark theme had the same defect in reverse. **The accent is now only ever a fill**: the left rule (where Discord actually puts it, which is what the previous top strip was asked about), the dot, the command token, the filled value chip, the aura. Where text sits on that fill the *foreground* is solved instead — and unlike the old approach that one cannot fail: solve the crossover where black and white are equally bad and it sits at relative luminance 0.1791, where the better of the two still measures **4.58:1**. Measured on the rendered page in light theme, `/patch notes` is now true `rgb(242,194,48)` at **12.53:1**.

**The six "colourless" commands became the most alive ones.** Six commands derive an accent per render instead of carrying a fixed one, and that fact was drawn as a hollow outlined dot, which reads as *unfinished* rather than as *true*. `utils/loadoutRender.js` has carried a `MP_CATEGORY_ACCENT` map all along — seven real weapon-category colours the bot genuinely answers in — so the page now reads it at build time: the derived six wear one quiet grey rather than a hollow outline, and **`/gunsmiths list` re-tints the entire panel to the category you pick**, because that is exactly what the bot will do. Choose LMG and the panel turns Grape Purple `#845EC2`. The page demonstrates its own sentence instead of asserting it, and the palette went from eight colours to fifteen.

**Searching "loadout" returned one of the three loadout commands.** The index matched the command, its purpose, its option names and its choice labels — everything the bot declares, none of which contains the word a player types. `/gunsmiths list` and `/dmz` are entirely about loadouts and matched nothing. Every command now carries a hand-written keyword vocabulary, gated by an oracle of real queries that asserts an **exact** set rather than a superset, because a search returning everything fails as badly as one returning nothing.

**Three pieces of chrome came off this page.** The "On this page" accordion no longer renders — the rail already is that navigation, and stacking both cost 107px above the fold under a 54px bar. The trademark disclaimer is gone (`pageFoot()` already had the variant; two other templates use it): it earns its place under a legal instrument and is noise under a command reference. And the stage's `min-height:60vh`, which existed to stop the footer moving, was buying that with a screenful of void under every short panel.

**Then a third review, and the honest finding is that several of its defects were mine from the second.** Adding Discord's own registered option description as "the help layer" did not remove the hand-written sentence it superseded, so an option printed its description **three times** — Discord's, then a near-identical hand-written one, then that one again in the free-text branch. The per-option prose layer is now deleted outright: Discord's `description` is what the client shows a reader a second later, so one authoritative sentence replaces three that agreed. The `IN DISCORD` line went with it — it restated the purpose line directly above it — and each command now carries up to three **facts a reader could not guess** instead: that weapon search matches partial words and updates live, that a blank `style` returns all nine formats, that `/help` answers privately by default.

**`visibility` is a real option again, and the page was calling a lie truth.** It had been filtered out of the option list and described in prose, and because the filter ran *before* the empty-check, `/invite` rendered "No options — just run it." while its one option sat in the footnote three lines below. It is a selectable option like any other and is now drawn as one.

**Every command card was loading with its own heading cut off.** `scroll-margin-top` had **zero** occurrences in the file — the rewrite dropped it — so every fragment jump parked the panel under a 54px fixed bar *plus* a sticky rail. It fired on all fourteen.

**The page now searches the weapon list the bot searches.** The site builds with no database, so `scripts/exportWeaponIndex.mjs` dumps weapon names, keys, categories and build counts into a committed JSON — **68 MP and 7 DMZ weapons** — which the page inlines. Typing "hol" finds Holger 26, and an exact match re-tints the whole panel to that weapon's own category colour: AK117 turns it AR Crimson, FENNEC Electric Gold, LOCUS Electric Blue. ⚠️ The artifact is the cost of that choice, so `scripts/weaponIndex.test.js` fails on a missing, malformed or implausibly small file — including a case proving the plausibility floor can reject the one-row index that the exporter's own first run produced from a wrong field name.

**Four of the eleven `/gunsmiths list` scopes made the card lose all colour.** `All MP builds`, `Meta — MP`, `Meta — DMZ` and `DMZ` have no entry in `MP_CATEGORY_ACCENT`, so the re-tint fell through to `removeProperty`. They now take the bot's own MP and DMZ identity colours, read out of `commands/manage.js`, with the two meta scopes held darker. The rail chip follows the live tint too, rather than staying grey while the card changed.

**Copy stopped refusing, and Clear appeared.** Disabling Copy while a required option was empty removed a legitimate action — copying the bare command so you can type the rest in Discord. And every token in the line is now a button that opens its own option, the way clicking an option pill in Discord opens its picker.

**The landing state leads with the commands, and it behaves differently on a phone.** Fourteen full cards — name, purpose, option chips — made the mobile landing **3292px, 4.1 screenfuls**, on the device most of these readers use. On mobile the cards collapse to a two-per-row grid of names, so all fourteen are visible at once, which the horizontally-scrolling rail above cannot do; the landing came back to **1934px**. The fold threshold that hid five of eleven scopes behind "+5 more" was 6, tuned for a layout that no longer exists; it is 12, and an open slot now spans both grid columns so a fifteen-item list uses the full width instead of one narrow column beside an empty one.

**Two accessibility gaps closed with it.** Filtering the index changed the list with no status message, so a screen-reader user got no signal that results had narrowed or emptied — there is now a polite `role="status"` region that is silent at rest and says "2 of 14 match" or names the miss. And a `:target` panel swap moved the viewport but no focus, so activating a command left the reader on the link while the stage changed behind them; the panels carry `tabindex="-1"` so the fragment moves focus into them, the same technique the skip link uses on `<main>`. Verified at a real 375px touch viewport with `pointer:coarse` actually matching: no horizontal overflow, every control at 44px, and the stage ordered *above* the index on a phone so a reader who is lost meets the ask index first.

**One CSS trap is worth the words, because it fails silently and reads as correct.** The sticky command line is `position:fixed` on a phone, and it was measured at `top:1268px` in an 812px window — painted, correct in the source, and nowhere anyone could see it. The card containing it animates on arrival, and an animation filling *forwards* leaves its final keyframe applied as a computed value: a final `transform: none` computes to the **identity matrix**, and a transform of any value — identity included — makes its element a containing block for every fixed descendant. Releasing the fill fixed it after the animation but not *during*, so every command switch threw the line off screen for 300ms. The arrival motion now lives on the heading block and the accent rule, neither of which has a fixed descendant, and the card animates opacity only.

`scripts/lib/commandCatalog.js` also now mirrors `help.js`'s own `detailCommands || staticCommands` precedence, added by #154. It changes nothing today — the built catalog is byte-identical either way — but reading only the coarse list would compute `gated` from an ungated parent, so a future subcommand carrying its own `requires` would be hidden in `/help` and **published on the website** with every gate green. Two new test cases, both verified to fail against the one-list version.

Also closed: `.github/workflows/deploy-site.yml` did not watch `commands/**` or the three new modules, so a command rename could have shipped a page that silently disagreed with the bot; `dior legal check` was found globbing the `public/legal/` directory deleted in the 2026-08-05 flattening, checking 2 files instead of 8 (filed cross-project — it lives in a separate repo); and the build's contrast audit only matched `:root[data-theme="light"]` **with** quotes, so an unquoted light block was never read at all — widening the matcher took it from 3 variables to 13.

## Pre-Release v3.50.0 — 2026-08-18 20:43 EDT (#158 · `f3e0303`) — the reflow-comments CI crash, and a `/help` wording pick that turned out to be a decision already made

A small follow-up session picked up two loose ends from the review-remnants plan, neither of them worth their own review-remnants session: a CI-only bug found (but not fixed) during Session 2, and a filed UX question that turned out not to be as open as it looked.

`scripts/reflow-comments.mjs`'s `externalCheck()` shelled out to `node --check /dev/stdin` (and `bash -n /dev/stdin`), which crashes on GitHub Actions' Linux runners with `ENOENT` on a `/proc/<pid>/fd/socket` path — Node's `/dev/stdin` resolution breaks when the underlying fd is a socket rather than a regular pipe, a quirk that's invisible on macOS and only ever fires for a file with a genuinely proposed change. Found live on PR #156's CI run, deliberately not fixed there to avoid scope-creeping a review-remnants PR into the reflow tooling itself. Fixed here with the identified workaround: `text` now writes to a real temp file (cleaned up in a `finally` block) instead of being piped through `/dev/stdin`. 6 new regression cases (27 total, up from 21) cover valid/invalid JS and shell syntax, temp-file cleanup, and a structural guard that no code line references `/dev/stdin` any more — a revert would fail that test even if syntax checking happened to still work locally.

`/help`'s "no options besides visibility" wording — filed from Session 1 as three inconsistent treatments needing a canonical pick — turned out to be two things, not one, on a closer look: the four single-command categories already use the correct shape (`renderCommandBlock()`'s per-command header), and the two admin pages' shared-footnote pattern isn't an inconsistency at all — it's Harkirat's own explicit 2026-08-10 decision to stop repeating the Options header per command specifically because it read as overwhelming. Applying "pick one style everywhere" would have silently reverted that. Surfaced before touching anything; folded into a broader `/help` design pass Harkirat already has planned, rather than treated as a standalone quick pick.

`npm test` green throughout (full suite). `docs:audit` clean on this branch's own commits.

## Pre-Release v3.49.0 — 2026-08-18 15:34 EDT (#157 · `b56d504`) — the SearchTerm buffer, and a shutdown race that finding #12 never actually closed

The third and last session of the review-remnants plan (`local/handoff/review-remnants-plan.md`, gitignored), closing finding #56 — the one finding the plan deliberately kept isolated in its own session rather than folding in beside unrelated work, since it directly intersects finding #12's shutdown-race fix.

`utils/eventStore.js`'s `SearchTerm` upsert was the one write in the event plane bypassing the `FLUSH_AT` buffer, issuing a standalone `updateOne` per closed search session. It now goes through a buffered `bulkWrite` — the same `FLUSH_AT`/idle-timer/`MAX_BUFFER` discipline the event buffer already uses — flushed through `flushSearchSessions()`, the same shutdown call site finding #12 hooked `flushEvents()` into.

Re-reading finding #12's fix fresh, rather than trusting it by reputation, surfaced a real defect in it: `installShutdownFlush()` and `utils/instanceLock.js`'s `releaseLock` both register listeners on the same `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`, and Node invokes every listener for one signal synchronously, back-to-back. `flushSearchSessions()`/`flushEvents()` splice their buffers the instant they're called — so whichever listener ran SECOND always found the buffers already drained by the first and resolved via pure microtasks, calling `process.exit()` before the first listener's real, macrotask-bound Mongo write could land. Finding #12 closed the race only for the narrower pre-`ClientReady` window where `releaseLock` is the sole listener — not the realistic post-`ClientReady` case where both coexist. Fixed by memoizing the shutdown flush into one shared promise, `flushAllForShutdown()`, that every listener on the signal now awaits instead of each independently re-invoking flush functions that are individually idempotent-but-fast-no-op on a second call.

**Live-verified against real local dev Mongo, not just `npm test`** — a real process shutdown is structurally outside what a unit test can exercise. A disposable harness (not committed) reproduced the pre-memoization race directly: a real `SIGTERM` with two independent listeners silently dropped the buffered write, confirmed absent via `mongosh`. The shipped fix landed the write across 4 repeated real `SIGTERM` runs against the actual `acquireInstanceLock()`/`installShutdownFlush()` code paths. 4 new pure-logic cases cover the buffered op shape, the `FLUSH_AT` auto-trigger, and the memoization itself (`scripts/eventStore.test.js`, 27 cases total, up from 23).

`npm test` green throughout (full suite). This closes the review-remnants plan except for finding #9 (`AnalyticsEvent` TTL), which stays a deliberately out-of-scope conditional item until mid-September 2026 per the already-settled retention decision.

## Pre-Release v3.45.0 — 2026-08-18 09:52 EDT (#153 · `88afe83`) — a full-branch code review, and 61 of its findings fixed same-session

A `/code-review max` pass over the entire `v3-pre-release` branch (47 commits, 319 files, 21,077 added / 12,219 removed lines vs `main`) surfaced 68 findings — nine ship-blockers, dozens of smaller correctness bugs, cleanup, and stale docs. This release applies 61 of them directly (14 in a first pass covering the ship-blockers and one-line data-integrity fixes, 47 more in a second pass covering the rest); 1 was deliberately left unfixed on an already-settled retention decision, 5 were deliberately skipped as needing a new architectural abstraction rather than a bounded fix, and 1 needed no action. Full report: `local/handoff/2026-08-18-v3-pre-release-code-review.md` (gitignored); status entry: `docs/db-deferred-list.md`.

The nine ship-blockers: `/gunsmiths list`'s Copy Code button could hand back a different build's Gunsmith code than the card on screen (fixed by resolving through the same scope-aware chain the card renders from); `models/SeasonalData.js`'s `draft.calendar` couldn't store `isDoubleCP`, so Promote to Live silently flattened every staged 2X CP event; `/draw calculator` rendered the un-doubled CP figure for every 2X pack; 22+ MP categories could make `/gunsmiths list`'s scope-choice registration throw with no try/catch around it, silently skipping ALL command registration; a transient Cloudinary error crashed the `/colors` Nameplate view via an unbound identifier; three admin-grant confirmations posted publicly instead of ephemerally; `/manage`'s purge-confirm and delete-confirm skipped the per-page permission re-check on the actual destructive step; `models/AnalyticsEvent.js` had no retention path and would eventually exhaust the free-tier Atlas cluster (left unfixed — see below); and `scripts/backupDb.sh`, the only backup this database has, aborted silently under `set -e` before its own error guard could ever print.

Beyond the ship-blockers: a full `/manage` subsystem dedup pass collapsed 24 duplicated `SeasonalData` fetch call sites and 3 copy-pasted bulk-delete confirmation scaffolds down to one shared helper each, plus similar consolidation for upsert/removal-by-title logic, the loadout mode↔page-key mapping, export-file replies, and the denial-message string; the instance-lock's startup guard closed a real TOCTOU race with an atomic claim; the roll-up job now re-touches its last-rolled day so a late-arriving event is never permanently uncounted, and fires on `ClientReady` in addition to the 24h heartbeat interval so a same-day double-deploy can no longer stall it indefinitely; all 41 timezone dropdown labels now derive their DST abbreviation live instead of baking in a fixed one (15 of 41 zones observe DST); and a cluster of Cloudinary/Discord-CDN cache-consistency bugs (a distinguishable error sentinel, a complete `rawContext` on every memoized entry, an in-flight render de-dup) closes the gap where a transient network blip could re-render and re-post an already-cached design.

Held, not fixed: `models/AnalyticsEvent.js`'s missing TTL (finding #9) — Harkirat already decided 2026-08-16 to defer the retention number until a month of real production fill-rate data exists; re-opening it as a new question would have re-litigated a settled call. Skipped, each needing a new architectural addition rather than a bounded fix in code this session couldn't click-test: the CP-currency/timezone picker's 4 duplicated site-pairs, `/help`'s page-builder rewrite, `cpPackages.js`'s return-value spread (its own test file reads it directly), a new buffer+flush cycle for `SearchTerm` upserts (would sit on the exact shutdown-race territory this same release just fixed), and a documented-load-bearing-ordering restructure in `colorPalette.js`'s cross-view refresh.

`npm test` green throughout; two existing tests were updated (not reverted) to match intentional behavior changes rather than the bugs they used to encode: `rollupStore.test.js`'s idempotency case now expects the last-rolled day to be re-touched, and `discordCdnAssetIndex.test.js`'s recovery-happy-path assertion now expects the recovered `discordMessageId` in the return.

## Pre-Release v3.44.0 — 2026-08-17 19:35 EDT (#152 · `4e004a5`) — recover storage-channel messages instead of orphaning them

A deleted Cloudinary resource used to permanently orphan its Discord storage-channel message and force a full re-render + duplicate upload on the next view, even though the exact bytes were still sitting in the channel — the same code that posted the message discarded its id instead of remembering it. Traced during a re-verification of an existing `docs/db-deferred-list.md` item ("does the grouped-upload path share the single-file path's orphan behavior?"); confirming the claim held wasn't a good enough answer, since the underlying data to do better was already sitting in the same upload response.

Adds a durable, Cloudinary-INDEPENDENT secondary index (`models/DiscordCdnAsset.js` + `utils/discordCdnAssetIndex.js`) — one row per rendered design, written alongside every storage-channel upload in BOTH the live per-view path (`utils/nameplateWebpCache.js`/`utils/decorationWebpCache.js`) and the bulk script's grouped path (`scripts/bulkCacheCollectibles.js`), so it survives a later Cloudinary-side deletion untouched. On a Cloudinary cache-miss, the index is checked before treating it as a cold render: if a record exists, the still-live `cdn.discordapp.com` bytes are re-fetched directly and re-uploaded to Cloudinary at the same `public_id`, restoring the cache and skipping the render pipeline's single most expensive phase (frame compositing + ffmpeg encode) entirely, then letting the existing palette self-heal re-derive what only Cloudinary ever held. `utils/discordCdnStorage.js`'s two upload functions now return the message id they were silently discarding.

Also fixes an adjacent bug found while wiring this in: `healPalette()` in both cache modules replaced Cloudinary's `context` wholesale on every palette heal (a Cloudinary `api.update` `context` write replaces the whole map), silently wiping `render_source`/catalog metadata each time — now merges onto the previously-read context instead of rebuilding it from scratch.

`utils/discordCdnAssetIndex.test.js` (11 cases covering the index and every recovery branch, including a partial-success-after-failure case) added to `npm test`. `docs/db-deferred-list.md`'s two related entries updated to describe the shipped fix rather than the accepted workaround.

## Pre-Release v3.42.0 — 2026-08-17 13:36 EDT (#150 · `0e8a990`) — a `--watch` restart race closes, and every Flaticon icon author gets credited

- **`node --watch` restarts no longer lose the race with the instance lock.** The dev-bot workflow (`node --watch --env-file=.env.dev index.js`) could kill the bot for the rest of a session: a restart kills the old process before its async Mongo lock release lands, so the new process reads a heartbeat that still looks fresh and wrongly refuses to start — silently, with the terminal still looking healthy. `utils/instanceLock.js`'s `acquireInstanceLock` now also checks whether the lock's pid is still alive on this host (`process.kill(pid, 0)`) before honoring a fresh heartbeat; cross-host locking (a local Mac vs. the prod VM) is untouched, since a remote pid can't be probed this way. Verified live: a genuine boot, a real concurrent-instance refusal (the guard still works), four rapid `--watch` restarts (zero false refusals, previously the exact failure), and the dead-pid-stale-lock edge case (an unclean exit now restarts instantly instead of waiting out the 30s staleness window).
- **`NOTICE` now credits all 11 Flaticon icon authors**, in Flaticon's required attribution format (its free tier requires attribution). 10 of 11 were verified live one-by-one via a real browser (Flaticon blocks bot fetches outright); `customicondesign_1`'s actual URL slug turned out to be `customicondesign-1` — hyphenated, despite the underscore in its own display name — which a naive derivation would have gotten wrong. The 11th, Magnific, is credited by name with no author link: Flaticon's own parent company recently renamed itself Freepik → Magnific too, which broke that individual author's profile URL on Flaticon's end.

## Pre-Release v3.41.0 — 2026-08-17 09:50 EDT (#149 · `ce87e72`) — `/invite` design pass, and a 95% smaller mascot

**`/invite` rebuilt from Harkirat's own mockup** (`local/invite_ui.json`). Two structural simplifications came out of it. The two explicit guild/user buttons collapse to **one `Invite` button on the bare chooser URL**, letting Discord's own Add App picker offer whichever install types the application has enabled — the platform does the branching, so the panel cannot drift from the Developer Portal's settings. And the fenced share block becomes a real **`Share Link` button**, whose handler replies with the raw `discord.com/oauth2` URL **and nothing else**: Discord unfurls its own authorization links into an app card, and a bare body makes "copy text" yield exactly the link.

**Five values in that mockup were resolved rather than copied**, because it was built live on the dev bot. The client_id and the `</help:…>` mention id were the **dev** application's; `flags: 36864` carried SUPPRESS_NOTIFICATIONS on top of Components V2; the `custom_id` was mockup-generated. The one that would have broken silently in production was the mascot: a **signed `cdn.discordapp.com` attachment URL** whose `ex=`/`is=`/`hm=` params expire within about a day — the exact failure this repo already fixed by re-hosting that asset, reintroduced by hand.

**The mascot now loads 95% smaller, and the fix was not the one asked for.** Harkirat asked whether PR #146's Cloudinary memoization could speed the mascot up. It cannot: that fix memoizes `cloudinary.api.resource()` **Admin API lookups** (138–470ms each) for runtime-resolved public_ids, and this URL is a constant — there is no lookup, so that cost is already zero. The real cost was **bytes**: a 2048×2048 source delivered with only `f_auto,q_auto` into an ~80-point thumbnail. Measured against the live CDN: **266,911 → 13,601 bytes at `w_256`, 94.9% smaller** (`w_160` = 7,143, `w_128` = 5,450, recorded as the further levers). ⚠️ That figure is the **origin fetch**; Discord serves message images through its own caching media proxy, so the win is on cold fetch and proxy ingest rather than a measured client-side render time. The URL also moves into new **`utils/brandAssets.js`** — it was a duplicate literal in `commands/help.js` and `commands/invite.js`, and the transform would otherwise have landed on one copy and left the other slow, invisibly.

**A `skipExpiry` opt-out at the `sendV2Payload` boundary**, defaulting off. `Share Link` is a real custom_id button, which normally re-arms the 10-minute idle-disable for the whole container — greying it out beside a still-live `Invite` link on exactly the public post the command exists to leave behind. The bar for this flag is *"nothing on this panel can go stale"*, not *"losing it is inconvenient"*; `/invite` qualifies structurally, since its handler answers with its own fresh token.

**`/invite` has no "Show Everyone" button, by decision** — Harkirat, on reviewing it: *"i don't actually want the show everyone button for it. they can just send the command again publicly."* The command already defaults to public and carries its own Share Link, so a third route to publishing it is redundant; `/help` dropped the same button on the same reasoning.

**It also closed a real bug, which is why it had already gone.** Auditing this branch found that the "Show Everyone" path defeated the new opt-out: `handlers/share.js` builds the public copy and sends it through `sendV2Payload` **itself**, without the flag — so a shared `/invite` armed the timer after all, and its Share Link greyed out ten minutes later on precisely the public post the command exists to leave behind. That shipped live in v3.40.0. Threading the flag through was rejected (share.js has only the message JSON, so it would need its own table of exempt commands — a second copy of the decision) and so was always-skipping there (a shared `/settings` panel genuinely should expire). ⚠️ **The bug later being solved some other way is not a reason to restore the button — the decision above stands on its own.**

**Staleness found and fixed:** `.claude/rules/interaction-router.md`'s handler roster listed `alerts` and `audit` — **both retired the previous day** — while omitting `bot`, `drawCalc` (never listed) and `invite`. Two removals and two additions cancelled out, so its **"Fourteen subsystems" count stayed accidentally correct while a fifth of the list was false**. The numeral is gone; the roster is now defined as whatever `handlers/*.js` contains.

## Pre-Release v3.40.0 — 2026-08-16 21:00 EDT (#148 · `f8959f3`) — `/invite`: one panel, both install paths

**New command: `/invite`.** Dioreo's own share surface, and the first place the bot presents its two install paths as a real choice rather than a single opaque "Add App" link. One Components V2 panel: a mascot hero, then **Add to a Server** (guild install — everyone in the server can use it, needs Manage Server, `permissions=0` because the bot holds zero standing guild permissions by design) and **Add to Your Account** (user install — the commands follow you into any server, DM or group chat), each explained in prose above a matching link button, with a Website button alongside. Carries the bot-wide `visibility` option, defaults **public** (the point of running it is to show other people), and offers "Show Everyone" when run hidden.

**Install URLs are now derived, not hardcoded — this fixed a latent bug.** New `utils/inviteLinks.js` resolves the application id off the live client at render time and builds all three URL shapes. `commands/help.js`'s install button previously carried the **production** client_id as a string literal, so the local dev bot's own help panel offered an install link for the production application — silent, and wrong. Both commands read the one helper now, so a second copy cannot drift.

**`/help` and `/invite` share Coral `#FF7D5C`.** They are the bot's two meta commands — about Dioreo itself rather than about CODM data — and both show the coral mascot, so they sit outside the one-colour-per-command scheme the content commands use rather than competing inside it. A first pass moved `/help` to Signal Green `#58D05A` (hue 121°, the dioreo.app `/commands` accent) so `/invite` could hold coral alone; Harkirat reversed that after seeing both live — *"scratch the green colour on /help, let's keep the coral colour for both."* Recorded in the rules file rather than erased, because the green has a paper trail that would otherwise read as an unfinished swap.

**The panel was condensed after a live review.** The first build explained each install path with a heading and two or three bullets; Harkirat's verdict was *"WAY too much info and noise."* It is now two lines — one per path — above the buttons, roughly a third of the original text and 10 components instead of 15. The cut caveats (Manage Server required, no permissions requested) are stated by Discord's own install dialog on the very next screen, so removing them lost nothing a user needed.

**Added a share path, which a command alone cannot provide.** Someone may want to *pass the link on* rather than install it themselves, so the panel ends with `https://dioreo.app/install` in a fenced code block — Discord renders a real copy affordance on those, whereas a link button can only navigate. It shares that short site route rather than a raw OAuth URL deliberately: the redirect already exists (built from the same client id, so it cannot drift), it survives the OAuth URL changing parameters, and it works **outside Discord entirely** — which is the half of `docs/ROADMAP.md`'s "Easy bot sharing" item no slash command can reach. A custom_id button was considered and rejected: it would re-arm the passive-expiry timer this panel was just freed from, killing the share control after ten idle minutes on exactly the public post it exists for.

⚠️ **Two things about `/invite` are deliberate and will read as bugs without this note.** It is **not wired into `/help`** — no directory line, no dropdown row, no detail page, no `cmd:` autocomplete — because the placement decision was deferred on purpose; the three options are filed in `docs/db-deferred-list.md`'s 🗂️ Queued. And its **"Add to Server" link is inert on production** until Guild Install is enabled in the Developer Portal at v3 launch, which is a per-application toggle no code can set. The dev application already has it on, and that flip is the same one the v3 launch step already tracks.

**Bug fix found while shipping this — link buttons were being disabled by the idle timer.** `utils/passiveExpiry.js` treated every type-2 component as interactive with no style check, so a link button counted toward arming the 10-minute idle-disable *and* got `disabled: true` when it fired. A link button carries no custom_id, fires no interaction and depends on no token — it cannot go stale, so disabling it is always wrong. **This was already live on `/help`**, whose **Website** and **Install Dioreo** buttons died after ten minutes. `/invite` surfaced it in its sharpest form: its public panel is link buttons *only*, so it armed a timer whose sole effect was to kill the install buttons on a message whose entire purpose is to be clicked later by whoever scrolls past. A panel with no non-link interactive component now arms no timer at all. Four cases added to `scripts/passiveExpiry.test.js` (22 total), and the guard was verified able to fail.

Two decisions the frozen spec left explicitly open, resolved here: the day key is UTC and includes the **year** (`'2026-08-16'`, not alertId/changeId's year-less `'Aug16'` — those retain for 30d/180d and can never see two Aug 16ths, a roll-up kept indefinitely can); and `distinctUsers` stores the day's bounded hash set (`userHashes`, cap 5,000) so a multi-day distinct-user figure can be a real set union — past the cap, `distinctUsersExact` flips false and the array is dropped rather than kept partial, since a partial set unioned with another day's would silently undercount.

**`scripts/analytics.mjs`** — the "read analytics outside Discord" half of §6. `summary [--days N]` prefers roll-ups and falls back to a live `AnalyticsEvent` query for any day not yet rolled up (today, by design, is never rolled up). `failed-searches [--limit N]` reads the `SearchTerm` aggregate stage 2 built. A read-only Atlas user for this script is filed as a reminder rather than built — creating one is an Atlas console action outside this repo's reach.

**Usage/Timing pages** gain an Export button, matching the shape Alerts/Changes already use (`buildUsageExport()`/`buildTimingExport()`, downloadable `.txt`).

## Pre-Release v3.35.0 — 2026-08-16 13:24 EDT (#143 · `a718c25`) — the bot starts recording what it actually does, and a raw user ID leaves the database

**Stage 2 of 4 of the observability layer** (design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-16-observability-layer-design.md`). Stage 1 made every log line say *what the user was doing*; this stage turns that same context into a durable record. Nothing anywhere recorded what users actually do — the `/gunsmiths` consolidation was decided with no usage data at all — and collection is the time-sensitive half: a panel can be built any month, but last month's data can never be collected retroactively.

**Three new collections.** `models/AnalyticsEvent.js` is one document per interaction: who (a **keyed hash**, never the Discord ID), where, which command and subcommand, how it was triggered, how it turned out, how long it took to acknowledge and to finish, how long each external dependency took, and a bounded `detail` bag. `models/SearchTerm.js` is a grouped aggregate carrying **no user linkage at all** — term, command, field, and counts. `models/BootRecord.js` is one row per process start, which is also where restart *count* comes from: `process.uptime()` reports the current process's age and cannot know how many times systemd restarted the unit, so counting boot rows is the answer the spec had wrong in an earlier draft.

**`utils/eventStore.js` (new) — the buffered writer.** Events accumulate in memory and go out in one `insertMany` on a 15-second timer or at 25 events, **except on `outcome === 'error'`, which flushes immediately** — the moment an event is most worth having is right before a crash that would discard the buffer. Every write is fire-and-forget and swallowed, the `utils/alertStore.js` idiom. **The response path never awaits a write**: a Mongo insert is 30–80ms against Discord's 3-second budget for zero user benefit. A SIGTERM handler flushes the last buffer, because systemd stops the unit on every deploy and the events immediately before a restart are among the most interesting there are. The size guard uses `estimatedDocumentCount()`, never `countDocuments()` — the latter is a full collection scan, so a guard protecting against a large collection would become a performance problem at exactly the moment it fired.

**Outcomes come from the guards that already existed** — they needed to *report*, not to be rewritten: the 600ms anti-spam cooldown (which previously left no trace anywhere, so a dead click was uncountable), `/manage`'s admin lock and its per-page `resolveAction` denial, `/admin`'s server-admin gate, and `/share`'s visibility-policy block. ⚠️ **The 45 `"interaction likely expired"` catches were deliberately NOT edited.** The design named seven of them in three files; the real count is 45 across 18 files, and hand-instrumenting each is 45 edits whose coverage decays the moment somebody writes the 46th. Instead the router wraps the interaction's own response methods once and observes the **rejection code** (10062/40060) — which catches every one of them, including the paths that have no such catch at all, and cannot decay.

**Autocomplete is debounced to one event per search session, not one per keystroke.** Discord fires an autocomplete interaction on every keystroke; at equal fidelity autocomplete would have been the large majority of a collection designed to grow forever while answering nothing. One open session per (user, command, field) flushes a single row carrying the keystroke count, the settled-on term and the result count. **The typed term is kept** — normalised and capped at 100 characters — because a search that returned nothing is the single best input to an alias table (`kilo` → `KILO 141`), and that fix is only findable if the term survives.

**Dependency timing wraps the clients, not the call sites.** `utils/cloudinaryClient.js` (new) is a transparent timing proxy that six modules now require in place of `require('cloudinary').v2`, covering ~18 SDK call sites with six one-line changes — and it never reads the rejected error object, because that object carries the account's live API key and secret. `utils/mongoTiming.js` (new) patches `Query`/`Aggregate.prototype.exec` rather than registering a Mongoose plugin with `pre`/`post` hooks, which has two failure modes this shape does not (a post hook that forgets `next()` deadlocks every query; a plugin registered late covers only some models). Vertex gets its one chokepoint in `utils/visionExtract.js`, with the token count folded onto the same dep row. Discord REST is timed in `utils/sendV2Payload.js`, the wrapper 30 modules already share.

🗑️ **`RenderTiming` is gone, and this is the part that makes the policy shorter.** It stored a **raw** `discordId`. `scripts/migrateRenderTimings.js` (new) migrates its rows with that ID replaced by the keyed hash, refuses to write if any raw ID survives into the migrated documents, and then drops the collection; `models/RenderTiming.js` and `utils/renderTiming.js` are deleted and their five `/colors` call sites now fold their fields into the interaction's own event via `mergeDetail()`. So this release **removes** a place a raw user ID was stored while adding one that structurally never holds one.

✅ **`installType` verified rather than assumed.** The spec listed guild-vs-user install as "believed available, check before the schema commits to it": `authorizingIntegrationOwners` (with `guildId`/`userId`) and `context` are both present on `BaseInteraction` in the installed **discord.js 14.27.0** typings, so the field is real.

🔴 **The project's highest-value test now exists and was proven able to fail.** `scripts/eventStore.test.js` (23 cases, wired into `npm test`) serialises a finished event document and **string-searches** it for the raw Discord ID, because the realistic regression is not somebody adding a `discordId` field — a schema review catches that instantly — but a `detail` value that happens to carry one or a `customIdPrefix` capture that grabs a segment embedding a user snowflake. The runtime uses the same predicate the test asserts on, and scrubs a document that trips it. The test was then run with the scrub disabled to confirm it actually fails; a falsifier that cannot fail manufactures confidence.

🐛 **A gap found in the enforcement this design was relying on.** `docs-audit`'s `privacy-model-coverage` check was named in the spec as the thing that would fail CI until the new model was disclosed. It would not have: it detects a per-user model by looking for a raw-ID field name, and `AnalyticsEvent` stores `userHash`. A model built entirely of per-user rows would have sailed past reporting green — the same **vacuous-pass** shape the check's own comment already warns about from the `GuildSettings.updatedBy` miss. `userHash` is now in its pattern; a keyed hash is still personal data under GDPR Recital 26.

⚖️ **`docs/legal/PRIVACY.md` goes to v1.12** (pending, taking effect alongside v1.11 at the v3 release). New §2.4b describes the interaction record in full — including, honestly, that the hash defeats someone holding the database alone but **not** someone holding the database *and* the key. §2.4a gains its own paragraph for the stage-1 attribution fields, which its existing wording actively contradicted (it said no log statement deliberately writes a user identifier, and that the logs are not indexed by user; a stable per-user hash on every line is both deliberate and precisely a user index). §7 states **indefinite** retention plainly rather than softening it, §9.4 explains that deletion is not guesswork here (hash the requester's ID, delete the matches), and the `RenderTiming` paragraph is removed. The "no analytics, no tracking, no profiling" claims in §0, §3 and Appendix C are made **precise** rather than deleted — no advertising, no ad-tech tracking, no third-party analytics SDK, no profiling or personalisation of any individual, all still true.

⚠️ **This merges but must NOT reach prod until PRIVACY v1.12 is in effect.** That is a **deploy** gate, not a merge gate — merged is not live, and this one is deliberately going to sit undeployed.

## Pre-Release v3.34.0 — 2026-08-16 12:30 EDT (#142 · `da002e0`) — interaction-context attribution: one edit, not 146

**Stage 1 of 4 of the observability layer** (design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-16-observability-layer-design.md`). Every structured log line now carries WHAT the user was doing and WHICH file actually logged it, without touching any of the ~146 existing `console.*` call sites.

**`utils/requestContext.js` (new)** wraps `handlers/router.js`'s `handleInteraction` in a Node `AsyncLocalStorage` context, established once per interaction: `{ interactionId, command, handler, userHash }`. `handler` is filled in per dispatch branch by a new `markHandler()` call placed right before each of the router's ~17 dispatch points (every subsystem, `/admin`, autocomplete, and the slash-command engine), so a log line from deep inside `handlers/manage/*.js` says `"manage"`, not just the raw `customId`. `userHash` is `HMAC-SHA256(ANALYTICS_HMAC_KEY, discordId)` — never the raw Discord ID, per the design's NEVER list. The key is a new 32-byte value in `.env`/`.env.dev` (deliberately different per environment, to avoid the dotenv-backfill trap that already bit the alert webhook once); it needs a password-manager backup, which is Harkirat's own action.

**`utils/logger.js`'s `patchConsole()` enrichment.** Every structured record now carries a stack-derived `component` (the file that actually called `console.*`, isolated by walking the frame past `logger.js`'s own call sites and past anything outside the repo root) plus either the live interaction context or, for non-interaction paths (the daily heartbeat, boot, gateway/shard diagnostics, Cloudinary cleanup in `bot/lifecycle.js`), a `context: 'lifecycle'` fallback tag — these are exactly the lines that matter most when the bot is unhealthy, so unlabelled was the wrong default. `Error.stackTraceLimit` is clamped to 5 during capture so a hot loop (e.g. `scripts/bulkCacheCollectibles.js`'s 925-item run, were it ever patched) doesn't pay for more stack frames than needed.

🐛 **Two real bugs found and fixed while verifying, both from the same root cause: this repo's own path contains a space** (`/Applications/Claude Code/Diors-Builds`). The first frame-parsing regex excluded whitespace from the file-path capture group and matched **zero frames on every single call in this checkout** — caught by a test asserting `component` actually resolves for a real repo file, not by inspection. The second version fixed the whitespace exclusion but let the capture group's greedy `.+` swallow the `"at functionName ("` prefix along with the path, so `filePath.startsWith(REPO_ROOT)` still failed. Fixed by anchoring on the LAST `(` in the frame line (or `"at "` when there is none) to isolate the path *before* matching it, rather than trying to exclude characters from a single regex.

**Verification:** `AsyncLocalStorage` propagation was the stage's explicit go/no-go gate per the design spec, so it's asserted directly rather than assumed — `scripts/requestContext.test.js` (new) proves context survives an `await` three levels deep, that two concurrent `runWithContext()` calls never leak into each other (the real router shape when two interactions arrive close together), and specifically that a listener registered on a plain `EventEmitter` *inside* `runWithContext()` still sees the context — reproducing the exact "across the discord.js event boundary" propagation risk the spec called out, since discord.js dispatches `interactionCreate` through an ordinary `EventEmitter`. `scripts/logger.test.js` gained matching coverage for the `lifecycle` fallback, the enriched interaction-context shape, and `component` resolution. Live dev-bot boot test + a deliberate thrown error, confirming attribution lands on a real interaction, not just in the synthetic test harness.

**Scope held deliberately narrow**, per the stage's own NEVER list: no new model, no Mongo collection, no privacy-policy change, no read surface. The event plane that actually *stores* any of this is stage 2.

## Pre-Release v3.33.0 — 2026-08-16 11:52 EDT (#141 · `898b3be`) — the global instruction file contradicted itself, and nothing had ever checked it

⚠️ **The main artefact of this release lives OUTSIDE the repo** — `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, the global instruction file loaded into every session of every project. It will not appear in the diff. Backups sit beside it (`CLAUDE.md.bak-2026-08-16T1145` pre-edit, `.bak2-preflow-2026-08-16T1150` pre-reflow) and should be deleted deliberately once reviewed.

**The finding is the contradiction, not the size.** The file asserted that `sequential-thinking` had *"zero invocations in all recorded history"* in one section, while a later section explicitly corrected that same claim to *"it has run TWICE, not never."* An always-on instruction file stating X and not-X is worse than a long one: whichever copy a reader hits first carries no signal that it was already refuted.

**A closed experiment occupied 5.4 KB of an always-on file.** The full sequential-thinking narrative — restriction, measurement window, logging obligation, close-out, verdict — remained verbatim across bullets marked *"THIS WINDOW IS CLOSED"*, *"CLOSED OUT"*, *"SUPERSEDED"* and *"no longer governs"*. Only the verdict governs. It was cut **bullet by bullet, not as a block** — because buried inside was a **STANDING CARVE-OUT** whose own text says it *survives* the window's close and *"must not be 'fixed' by deleting it."* A bulk deletion would have silently removed a live authorisation the completeness-sweep hook depends on. The provenance was not lost: it already exists twice in this repo (`local/mcp-observation-log.md` and the dated protocol spec), and the compacted text now points at both.

🔴 **Deleting self-annotating text orphans its annotations, and the orphans read as confident sentences.** Removing those bullets left three dangling cross-references in the *surviving* prose — "the bullet below is retained as the historical record", "the expiry clause below required", "SURVIVES the window's close" — each pointing at text that no longer existed. Reflow passed, structure was conserved, every rule survived; **only reading the survivors caught it.** Both remaining bullets were rewritten to stand alone.

**Soft-wrap is a global convention, and the global file had never been reflowed** — 45% of its prose lines continued a sentence onto the next, the exact searchability defect the 2026-08-08 tree-wide pass fixed. Demonstrated with a falsifiable case rather than asserted: the phrase *"and a false negative is far more expensive"*, from the file's own rg-completeness warning, matched **0 times before and 1 after**. Reflowed with `scripts/reflow-prose.mjs` after proving it on a copy first — line 1 is `@RTK.md`, an import read by line structure that a reflow could have folded into a paragraph.

**Verified by exit code, not summary text.** 24/24 governing rules present afterwards; word delta across the reflow exactly **0**; `@RTK.md` intact on line 1; no dangling references; `reflow --check` exit 0 on both the global file and all 91 memory files. **35,037 → 29,208 bytes (−17%)**, every removed byte justified by its own text saying it no longer governs.

**Also filed:** the gate gap this exposed — `docs:reflow` resolves its file list from `git ls-files`, so the memory store and the global CLAUDE.md are invisible to `npm test`. The store passed clean at 91/91, so the convention is holding by discipline; nothing would report when it stops.

## Pre-Release v3.32.0 — 2026-08-16 11:28 EDT (#140 · `f32be5b`) — the memory index gets 24% smaller without losing a single memory

**`MEMORY.md` was at 22,868 of its 25,000-byte budget (91%)** and past the SessionStart advisory line. It is the only auto-loaded memory file, so its size is a tax on every session — and the previous session had already had to route around it, folding new facts into an existing memory purely to avoid adding an index line that might not fit. That is the wrong default: it pushes unrelated facts into whichever file happens to have room.

**Now 17,369 bytes (69%) — 5,499 saved — with all 90 entries and all 90 files retained.** Nothing was deleted. Verified in both directions: every file on disk is linked from the index, and every index link resolves to a file.

**The diagnosis is the useful part.** This was never a "too many memories" problem. 78 of 90 index entries exceeded the 150-char guideline and carried **8,113 characters of excess** — narrative detail that had accumulated in the hooks over many sessions and belonged in the topic files, which are read on demand rather than loaded every session. The longest single entry was 891 characters. Trimming the hooks recovered the space with no loss of recall.

⚠️ **The `feedback_*` memories were deliberately exempted** from the consolidation skill's "retire dated files / drop what is easy to re-find" step. They record corrections and working agreements that cannot be re-derived from the repo, which is exactly what makes them worth the bytes.

**Two stale facts were corrected in passing**, which is the consolidation's other job: the `/gunsmiths` entry still claimed "not merged/deployed" after it shipped as v3.29.0 ([#137](https://github.com/HarkiratMangat/dioreo/pull/137)), and the `/manage` decomposition still read as a live four-stage project after all four stages closed on 2026-08-15.

## Pre-Release v3.31.0 — 2026-08-16 11:02 EDT (#139 · `1da506b`) — the observability layer is designed, the database has a real name, and backups exist at all

**A design session, plus two operational findings it turned up that could not wait.** No bot behaviour changes here; one new script and one production migration do.

**`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-16-observability-layer-design.md`** closes three roadmap items as a single layer rather than four systems: richer in-bot logging (line 48), usage analytics (line 132), and the admin `/status` command (line 49). Three planes — Cloud Logging for diagnostics, one new Atlas collection for events, the existing `AlertLog`/`ChangeLog` untouched — with **one document per interaction** carrying usage, timing, outcome and dependency calls together, because a usage row and a timing row turned out to be the same row. Identity is `HMAC-SHA256` of the Discord ID under a key held outside the database and never stored raw; `guildId` stays raw. Attribution comes from an `AsyncLocalStorage` context set once in the router plus a stack-derived component, which is one edit rather than 146 and cannot decay as new modules are written. The read surface is `/bot analytics` (Health · Alerts · Changes · Usage · Timing) and `/bot access`, retiring `/alerts` and `/audit`.

🔴 **A premise that had blocked `/status` since 2026-07-20 was measured and found false.** `docs/ROADMAP.md` line 49 asserted the VM's service account could write Cloud Logging but not read it back. It runs as `435048837454-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com` with scope `cloud-platform` and role `roles/editor` — 11,974 permissions including `logging.logEntries.list` and `monitoring.timeSeries.list`. The bot can read its own logs *and* Cloud Monitoring via ADC with no role change. The false claim is struck through in place rather than deleted, with the measurement beside it, because a session reading the old wording would have inherited the wrong conclusion. The opposite finding — `roles/editor` also grants `logging.logs.delete`, so a compromised bot could erase its own audit trail — is filed and explicitly coupled to the spec.

**`scripts/backupDb.sh` — the only backup this database has.** Atlas M0 provides no automated backups at all, so a gap in running this is a gap with no recoverable copy. One gzipped archive per run into the gitignored `local/db-backups/`, newest 14 retained. It never prints `MONGODB_URI`, and it **verifies the archive instead of trusting the exit code** — `mongodump` can exit 0 having written an unusable stub, and a backup you believe in but cannot restore is worse than a missing one. Not yet scheduled.

**The production database was named `test`** — Mongoose's default, because `MONGODB_URI` carried no path segment — and is now **`diors-builds`**, pairing with the dev database `diors-builds-dev`. No code changed: the name lives entirely in the URI, and `index.js` already reads `mongoose.connection.name` for its boot log, which made that log the verification. Stopped the bot, dumped quiesced, `mongorestore --nsFrom 'test.*' --nsTo 'diors-builds.*'`, cut over both `.env` files, restarted. ~2 minutes of downtime. `test` is deliberately retained as a rollback.

**Verified, not assumed.** Both databases reported an identical 939 objects / 7 collections / 15 indexes / 288,815 bytes; the boot log printed `MongoDB (…/diors-builds)`; and `botinstances` re-populated in the new database, proving writes land there and not merely reads. ⚠️ The 940→939 delta was explained rather than waved off — it is the `botinstances` singleton lock, released on shutdown. The fresh copy also reclaimed ~600 KB of WiredTiger fragmentation (28 KB + 168 KB indexes, against 307 KB + 487 KB).

**Storage, now measured rather than estimated.** 776 KB of M0's 512 MB — 0.15%. `avgObjSize` is 307 bytes, which independently validates the spec's per-event estimate, and **indexes run 1.7× the data**, making index count the largest single lever on when the ceiling arrives. Harkirat's call: stay on the free tier and let the first month of real fill rate set the retention horizon rather than guessing it now.

## Pre-Release v3.30.0 — 2026-08-15 23:06 EDT (#138 · `0d88ba5`) — collectible cache-channel embeds redesigned, and their Cloudinary ids renamed to Discord's own naming

**The cache-channel message layout, specified by Harkirat to the character.** The description (`label`) is now a **blockquote beside the image** instead of a `-# **Description:**` footnote — it is the one human sentence in the block and was buried among machine identifiers. Collection, group and variant all left the per-variant footnotes for the headings: `## <design> — __<collection>__`, then `**N Variants** — **\`Blue\` · \`Red\`**` for a multi-variant design, then `### <display name> — \`#79E4E3\`` per variant (the label is not repeated — `displayName` already ends in it). Dimensions/frames/size moved off the heading onto the `Rendered` line, in bold, which frees the heading to carry the variant's colour swatch.

**The base SKU is conveyed by ORDER, not by a line of its own.** It is always some variant's own SKU, so printing it spent a line on a 19-digit number the reader cannot use; instead `catalogGrouping.js` promotes the base variant to the front of every group. Sorted there rather than in the message builder so the ordering survives `chunkVariants()` and the render order, the header's label list and the container's accent colour (taken from `renders[0]`) can never disagree about which variant is primary. It was already true by accident of catalog order for every group checked — this makes it guaranteed. **SKU is its own line** — tacked onto the end of the Cloudinary line it read as part of the url, which Harkirat called out on the fallback layouts too (both `nameplateWebpCache.js` and `decorationWebpCache.js` got the same split). A single-variant design gets no `###` heading and no dividers at all; the `##` header already names it.

Decorations keep Section+thumbnail and nameplates keep the full-width Media Gallery — a nameplate is a wide banner that reads badly shrunk into a Section's small square accessory. Both shapes cost exactly 4 components per variant, which is what `catalogGrouping.js`'s `COMPONENTS_PER_VARIANT` already assumes, so the message cap is unchanged; a new test asserts a full-size message stays under Discord's recursive 40-component ceiling.

**Cloudinary public ids are now `<group-name>-<variant-label>`** (`utils/collectibleCacheKey.js`) — Discord's own naming structure for a design with colour variants, read straight off the catalog instead of derived from the `asset` path. `/dev_nameplate_webp/nameplates-eternal-damnation-1533919389806493928-black` becomes `/dev_nameplate_webp/eternal-damnation-blue`; decorations get the same treatment (`/dev_decoration_webp/lord-of-the-dead-red`), which their bare asset hash never allowed before. A design with no variants is just `/dev_nameplate_webp/all-bark-all-bite`. The palette name left the key entirely — the catalog carries exactly one palette per SKU, so it pinned down nothing the group+variant pair did not.

**The live path now resolves the catalog to compute that id, and this is load-bearing rather than an optimization.** Discord's profile payload never carries `group_name`/`variant_label`, so `resolveNameplateWebp`/`resolveDecorationWebp` look the SKU up (`lookupCatalogEntry`, memoized per sku including negative results) before the cache lookup. Without it a live equip would compute a `legacy-` id, miss the bulk-cached render entirely and re-render from scratch — defeating bulk pre-caching, and breaking the `render_source: 'fallback'` heal-in-place path, which finds nothing when the two paths disagree. An uncatalogued design still gets `legacy-<name-or-asset>`.

**Two defects were caught by checking rather than by review, and neither was a syntax or logic error.**
- **Rendering the real Underworld group** — not the unit tests — exposed the description printing **twice** on every single-variant design: its heading lines were folded into the header block and then emitted again in the variant loop. The tests asserted the header *contained* the description but never that it appeared *exactly once*; that assertion now exists, across both kinds and both shapes.
- **Uniqueness of the new id was computed over the whole 925-SKU catalog before the key was changed**, globally rather than per-collection, since the folder is flat and two collections owning a same-named design would have collided: 262 nameplates → 262 distinct ids, 663 decorations → 663 distinct ids, 0 collisions. `scripts/collectibleCacheKey.test.js` re-runs it against the real JSON.

⚠️ **The 8 already-cached dev entries were reset to `pending` in the same change.** The public id is the cache key, so renaming it orphans everything stored under the old name — and those rows claimed `cacheStatus: 'cached'`, which would have made the bulk script skip them forever against ids nothing can find. They do not self-heal. Prod holds zero collectible renders, so nothing there is affected. The 8 superseded Cloudinary resources are now unreferenced and can be purged separately.

**Verification.** `npm test` exits 0. The layout was rendered end-to-end against the real dev catalog and diffed against Harkirat's written spec, not eyeballed from the code.

## Pre-Release v3.29.0 — 2026-08-15 21:56 EDT (#137 · `ceb7f8f`) — `/gunsmiths` consolidates nine loadout commands into two

`/all` and the eight per-category MP loadout commands (`/ar`, `/lmg`, `/marksman`, `/secondaries`, `/shotgun`, `/smg`, `/sniper`) — never real files in `commands/`, always dynamically built in `bot/registry.js`, and a standing trap for any sweep of that folder — are now `/gunsmiths search` (MP weapon lookup, fuzzy autocomplete) and `/gunsmiths list` (11 named scopes: 7 categories, All MP builds, Meta MP, Meta DMZ, DMZ). `/dmz` stays standalone. Ten loadout commands become two.

One shared scope descriptor `{mode, category, metaOnly}` (`utils/loadoutScopes.js`) drives every browsable set — a category view, meta, and DMZ are the same scoped card browser reached two ways: `list`'s named choices, or "sticky" category rows inside `search`'s autocomplete (an empty box shows all 7 categories, replacing the discoverability `/smg` used to offer). One shared weapon-lookup path (`utils/loadoutLookup.js`) replaces the previously duplicated logic in `commands/dmz.js` and `handlers/router.js`'s ~114-line MP fallback, which is deleted entirely along with its own duplicate announcement-delivery call site.

The whole shape is forced by one Discord rule: a command with any subcommand may carry no top-level options — which is why there is no `category:`/`mode:` option pair anywhere (a pair can combine into a meaningless state like DMZ-plus-a-category) and every browsable set is instead one whole named `scope:` choice.

**Task 1 was a real spike, not ceremony.** The whole registry approach depended on discord.js allowing a nested subcommand option's choices to be mutated with `setChoices()` after the builder is already constructed — untested going in, with a documented async-factory fallback ready in case it failed. It didn't: `toJSON()` still reports top-level option types as `[1]` (subcommand-only) after mutation.

Followed ADD-before-DELETE strictly: `/gunsmiths` was registered and verified live (clean dev-bot boot, no fault log) before the nine old commands and the router fallback were deleted, since the dev bot runs `node --watch` and a wrong order would have left it with no MP loadout lookup at all mid-deployment.

**A post-implementation sweep found and fixed real defects the deletion left behind**, none caught by the automated suite because none were syntax or logic errors: two comments in `bot/registry.js`/`handlers/router.js` that illustrated their reasoning with "the eight per-category weapon commands" after those commands no longer existed; a stale, actively-inverted warning in `.claude/rules/legal-site.md` that used to correctly insist those seven commands were real and invisible to a naive grep; and — the most consequential — the public site's homepage (`dioreo.app`) animates a typewriter that types real slash commands, and its data literally included `/ar`, `/smg`, `/lmg`, `/marksman`, `/sniper`, `/shotgun`, `/secondaries` (`scripts/buildLegalPages.js`'s `CMD_JS`). Fixed to type `/gunsmiths search`/`list` instead, and `public/` rebuilt to match.

Also ships: `/help`'s Gunsmiths page rewritten for the two-subcommand surface (retired-command names like `smg`/`ar` now alias to `/gunsmiths` rather than dead-ending), a non-silent fix for `buildCategoryBrowseRow`'s old silent-truncation-past-25-weapons bug (found in passing, fixed since the code was already being touched), and doc/rule-file/memory-store updates across `CLAUDE.md`, four rule files, `ROADMAP.md` (reconciling three previously-overlapping backlog items that all turned out to be the same feature), and the project memory store.

⚠️ **Two things deliberately NOT done, at Harkirat's explicit request** (unavailable to check live at merge time): the 14-step interactive Discord click-test (nothing automated can prove Discord accepts the registered JSON, that autocomplete orders correctly on a real client, or that a `gsb~` button actually fires), and a live preview of the rewritten `/help` Gunsmiths copy before merging (the prior page was built from Harkirat's own mockup; this one wasn't shown to him first). Both filed in `docs/db-deferred-list.md`.

**Verification.** `npm test` and `npm run docs:audit` both exit 0 at every commit checkpoint (11 commits); dev-bot boot verified clean registration both before and after the deletion; `scripts/gunsmithsCommandShape.test.js` and `scripts/loadoutRenderSnapshot.test.js` are new, falsifier-proven regression tests.

## Pre-Release v3.28.0 — 2026-08-15 19:16 EDT (#136 · `06cf38e`) — `/draw calculator` ships

`/draw calculator` — tells a player how much more CP they need to finish a lucky draw, and the cheapest real-money way to buy it. Two pure engines: `utils/drawCost.js` slices `DRAW_DATA`'s existing per-pull arrays; `utils/cpPackages.js` holds the six-package table (loaded from the committed 41-currency price file, never hand-typed) and a DP purchase optimizer with a cheapest-money and a least-waste pass. A two-stage Components V2 panel sits on top, entirely stateless via the `customId` — no model, no cache, except one deliberate exception: `UserPreference.cpCurrency`, disclosed in `PRIVACY.md` in the same commit that added it.

`commands/drawCalculator.js` deliberately exports no `data` — the `calculator` subcommand lives on `commands/drawprices.js`'s existing builder instead, since `bot/registry.js` keys command registration by `data.name` and a second file exporting `setName('draw')` would silently overwrite the first. Verified live with the real `loadCommandModules()`: exactly one `draw` command registers, carrying both subcommands.

**Two real bugs in the build plan's own pasted optimizer code, fixed before shipping rather than transcribed:** the DP never actually threaded the `currency` parameter through its price lookups (it would have silently priced every storefront the same, defeating the entire point of the 41-currency table), and `maxTransactions` was documented but never enforced (the DP's unconstrained optimum for a 5,000 CP shortfall in CAD is 63 separate $0.99 purchases). Both fixed and pinned with a regression test reproducing the design spec's own CAD worked example exactly.

A post-build adversarial review (Task 9.5, sequential-thinking) found three more real issues: the results headline showed the raw remaining-CP figure instead of the balance-netted shortfall, contradicting the line directly below it; the budget-mode modal collected a "Current CP balance" field the budget-mode result never read (silently discarded input); and an out-of-range target pull silently clamped to "finish the draw" instead of rejecting, inconsistent with the adjacent `pullsDone` field's own strict validation. All three fixed and verified.

Also ships: `isDoubleCP` on `SeasonalData.calendar[]` (a 2X CP event flag, set via a 5th field on the existing Calendar Add/Edit modals rather than a new registry action, since it's a property of the same entity those actions already edit) and its calendar-detection logic; the `/help` entry; and `.claude/rules/draw-prices.md`'s new section documenting every trap a future session would otherwise re-derive.

⚠️ **Two disclosed, deliberate gaps, not silent ones.** Budget mode only accepts a CP amount — the "convert a dollar figure through the optimizer first" half of the design's decision 10 isn't built. And this build was not click-tested live in Discord — no Discord client was available this session; verification instead used mock interactions against the real local dev Mongo (schema persistence round-trips, the seven-pull-draw and out-of-range-target-pull modal-validation regressions, every handler branch dispatching through its correct typed check) plus repeated clean dev-bot boots.

**Verification.** `npm test` and `npm run docs:audit` both exit 0 at every commit checkpoint (13 commits); `npm run site` re-run after the `PRIVACY.md` change, `public/privacy.html` rebuilt and committed. CI `syntax-check` passed on the PR.

## Pre-Release v3.27.0 — 2026-08-15 17:22 EDT (#135 · `63009d9`) — two guards built from this session's own misses, and a worktree finding

Enforcement only: no product behaviour changes.

**Two new hooks, both advisory and both proven.** `gate-truncation-guard.sh` fires when a gate (`npm test`, `docs:audit`, `docs:reflow`, a `scripts/*.test.js`) is piped straight into `tail`/`head` without `$?` or `PIPESTATUS` being captured — a pipeline exits with its *last* command's status, and these gates print their ERROR block **above** the trailing summary, which counts checks that RAN rather than checks that PASSED, so a truncated view reads exactly like a clean run. `untracked-doc-guard.sh` fires when a docs gate runs while untracked `.md` files exist, because `reflow-prose.mjs` and docs-audit both resolve their file list from `git ls-files` and cannot see a new document at all — the gate reports a healthy count over the corpus it *can* see.

**Both enforce rules that were already written down and violated anyway by the session that wrote them**, which is this repo's stated trigger for promoting prose to a hook: the truncation rule is recorded verbatim in `feedback_wrong_reference_beats_stale_one`, and it still hid a real `doc-frontmatter` failure across two commits. Each carries a `.test.sh` wired into `run-all-tests.sh` (28 hook tests now), and the truncation guard was confirmed firing on a **real tool call** — a pipe test proves the script works, never that the hook fires.

**Two practices documented rather than hooked**, because they are judgement and not mechanism: prove a tool on a KNOWN case before trusting it on unknown ones (an extractor was asserted against three real price tables before being run on 68 unknown storefronts — the only reason "70 of 71 succeeded" carried weight), and re-verify data that crossed from tool output into a file by hand. Both live in the global CLAUDE.md and as cases in `feedback_verify_before_claiming`.

🔴 **A `[P1 · M]` bug filed, and it is the interesting one.** In a worktree session, every `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`-based hook `cd`s to the **worktree** and reads git state there — not the tree the work is actually happening in. Nine git-reading gates therefore go silently blind, and a blind gate is indistinguishable from a passing one. Proven rather than inferred: the same hook, identical stdin, fires under `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<main repo>` and is silent under `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<worktree>`. It also explains an inconsistency that made this hard to notice — hooks carrying a hardcoded `cd` fired correctly all session while the resolved ones did not, so the gate set looked alive. **Filed rather than fixed:** whether a worktree session should be governed by the worktree or by the tree it edits is a real decision affecting 27 registrations, and hardcoding the path everywhere would re-create the existing `[P1 · XS]` non-Mac tag-hook bug.

**Also filed `[P3 · XS]`:** `timestamp-check.test.sh` has a time-flaky boundary case that fails intermittently with no code change — observed failing once, then passing three consecutive re-runs with an empty `git diff` on both files. A gate that fails for unrelated reasons teaches people to re-run until green, which is how a real failure gets waved through.

**Verification.** `npm test` exit 0, `npm run docs:audit` exit 0 with no ERROR block, both new suites green (10 and 8 proofs, including the silent cases that keep them from becoming noise).

## Pre-Release v3.26.0 — 2026-08-15 16:43 EDT (#134 · `25dcd25`) — `/draw calculator` designed, and CP prices captured for 41 currencies

Design-only: the spec and implementation plan for a lucky-draw cost calculator, plus the price data its optimizer cannot work without. No runtime code ships here.

**The feature.** `/draw calculator` answers the question players actually arrive with — *"I've done two pulls on this draw, how much more do I need, and what should I buy to get there without wasting money?"* Two independent pure engines: `utils/drawCost.js` slices the existing `DRAW_DATA` per-pull arrays, `utils/cpPackages.js` holds the package table and a DP purchase optimizer. Neither imports the other. A two-stage Components V2 panel sits on top, and all wizard state rides in the `customId` — no model, no persistence, which is a privacy decision as much as an architectural one (storing a CP balance would need a `PRIVACY.md` Appendix A entry). The single deliberate exception is `UserPreference.cpCurrency`, and the plan's Task 4 carries the matching PRIVACY obligation.

**`docs/reference/cp-package-prices.json` + `.md`** — the six in-game CP bundles priced in **41 currencies across 70 locales**, captured from the official CODM web store. This exists because Apple and Google assign price points **directly per storefront** — tier-locked, not rate-locked — and the tiers are **not proportional to one another**. Measured: **in 17 of the 41 currencies "buy the biggest pack" is wrong.** In NOK and SEK the *smallest* 80-CP pack is the best value in the store; PLN and HUF peak at a middle tier. Only 24 currencies (USD, GBP, JPY, BRL among them) are monotonic. That is the whole argument for solving rather than publishing a rule of thumb.
