**Two corrections caught before they could ship, both now pinned by tests in the plan.** (1) The 2X CP event doubles the **base**, not the advertised total — the store number already folds in the normal bonus (10,800 CP is 8,000 base +35%), so during an event that package yields 16,000, not 21,600; the first draft was wrong by 5,600 CP at the top tier. (2) An earlier draft claimed package prices were identical worldwide with only the currency label changing via FX. They are not, and that framing would have produced wrong purchase advice everywhere outside USD.

**Extraction method, for whoever re-crawls it.** Prices come from the store page's embedded JSON payload field `publisherPrice`, never from rendered display text — formatting varies by locale (`de-de` renders `99,99 €` with a trailing symbol and comma decimal; `ja-jp` uses `¥160` with no decimals) and an early regex over display strings silently returned partial data for `de-de`. ⚠️ `hasDiscount` is unreliable and reads `false` on visibly discounted items, so `publisherPrice` is taken unconditionally. The web store's CP *quantities* are web-exclusive and differ from in-game (88 vs 80, 460 vs 420, …) while the price points are identical, so bundles map by ascending tier position and never by CP amount. All eight traps are documented in the companion `.md`.

**Also restores a lost record.** `v3.24.0`'s CHANGELOG heading was missing entirely, so its whole body had been reading as part of v3.25.0's entry; it is restored with its real PR and hash, and v3.25.0's own `(#TBD)` is backfilled. `docs-audit` did not catch this, and the reason is now fixed rather than filed. `summary-orphan` exists for exactly this failure mode but reads CHANGELOG-SUMMARY as its reference list — and SUMMARY is deliberately not written during pre-release, so for the whole v3 line it had nothing to compare against; its heading regex also matches `## vX.Y.Z` but never `## Pre-Release vX.Y.Z`. A new **`devlog-orphan`** ERROR check reads DEVLOG headings instead, since DEVLOG *is* maintained through pre-release, and matches both heading forms. Its self-test caught a defect in the check itself on the first run — a vacuous pass, because the test fixture's DEVLOG entry carried no version stamp — which is precisely what `docs-audit.test.mjs` exists to do; the fixture now carries one, and all 69 checks are proven capable of failing.

**Verification.** Extraction reproduced all three price tables Harkirat supplied from his own stores (`en-us`, `en-ca`, `en-ie`) exactly; ten further rows (JPY, NOK, TRY, ZAR, MXN, CHF, PKR, HUF, COP, KWD) were re-fetched live and compared against the committed file *after* transcription, because hand-copying 41 rows is exactly where a silent error hides. Structural checks: 41 currencies, 70 locales, no duplicate locale mappings, every row six strictly-ascending prices. `npm test` green, `npm run docs:audit` at zero errors.

## Pre-Release v3.25.0 — 2026-08-15 13:37 EDT (#133 · `3962df4`) — a bugs-fix batch: /colors wording, /manage guides + rename, /help aliases, timezone search

Eighteen small-to-medium bug reports worked through in one session (screenshots + a written list), spanning `/colors`, `/manage`, `/help`, and `/settings`.

**`/colors`.** "Global Profile" → "Main Profile" everywhere (heading, the switch button's label, the loading placeholder) — the old wording read like it meant something different from "your own profile as opposed to a server one," which it didn't. The "Colors From Your X @user" heading became the possessive "@user's X Colors" (the old form read ambiguously once a mention followed "Your" directly). The "Switch below…" hint was reworded for clarity. Refresh Colors' confirmation message now opens with a real `###` heading instead of an inline bolded emoji line, and its closing hint switched from `-#` small-text to italics — the old hint used the identical small-text style as the "Refreshed X:" row labels directly above it, so the two blurred together visually.

**`/manage`.** Manage Admins and Announcement — the two pages with zero Bulk Format Guide coverage — each got a real guide topic (`utils/manageGuides.js`). The `data_for` slash option was renamed to `content` — the fourth attempt (`page`→`section`→`data_for`→`content`), after Harkirat confirmed the first three all failed the same test: none of them named the actual thing being picked, a data entity. Both the `content` choices and the in-panel `mng_pagesel` dropdown now share one consistent ordering (content pages → season actions in the order you'd actually touch them → admin pages → guide) — they used to disagree with each other, which was the real "feels scattered" complaint, not the number of selection surfaces.

**`/help`.** `cmd:` now resolves keyword aliases, not just literal command names — "server"/"owner" → `/admin`, "database"/"data" → `/manage`, and a comparable list for every other static command. Fixed a real bug: the Bot Admin detail page rendered all three admin commands' full writeups unconditionally, regardless of the viewer's actual per-command access — an admin granted only `/alerts` could still read the complete `/manage`/`/autobuild` documentation. A guide-topic dropdown was added to that same page (manage-gated, re-checked server-side) so a `/manage` guide is reachable without leaving `/help`. The redundant "`/admin` *(Admin)*" heading suffix was dropped, and one literal name in the slash description was replaced.

**`/settings`.** The Calendar Events default-preference toggle was silenced per direct request — commented out rather than deleted, in case the preference returns. `/calendar`'s own `view` option is now the sole (one-off, unsaved) way to pick Active/Upcoming. `scripts/clearCalendarEventFilter.js` cleared the 17 stored values that existed. The timezone dropdown expanded from 15 hardcoded zones to 40, each carrying city/country/abbreviation aliases (`utils/timezoneData.js`), reachable via the dropdown's direct picks or a "Search for your city…" modal that fuzzy-matches anything not in the quick list — Discord's own select menu caps at 25 options, so a bigger list can only ever be searched, never all shown at once.

**A gap the session's own audit caught before it shipped:** the timezone search modal was first built from raw snake_case API JSON; this bot's `showModal()` calls all use discord.js's `ModalBuilder`/`ActionRowBuilder`/`TextInputBuilder` classes instead (see `buildSearchModal` in `commands/manage.js`), and the raw form would very likely have thrown at runtime. Caught and fixed via a self-audit pass before merge, along with two stale rule-doc bullets (`.claude/rules/models.md`, `design-decisions.md`) still describing the Calendar Events toggle as live, and `/help`'s own Preferences description still advertising "calendar filter" as something `/settings` covers.

**Verification.** Full `npm test` green (docs-audit self-test's 68 checks, every hook self-test, every existing suite including `refreshNotice.test.js` — updated to match the Refresh Colors wording rework), `scripts/manageActions.test.js` (59 actions) and `scripts/handlerRouting.test.js` (14 handlers) both green after the `/manage`/`/help` routing changes, `npm run docs:audit` at zero errors. Not yet live-click-tested on the dev bot — filed alongside the existing LIVE CLICK-TEST OWED entry in `docs/db-deferred-list.md`.



## Pre-Release v3.24.0 — 2026-08-15 12:38 EDT (#132 · `6cc1400`) — DB change log and `/audit`

Stage 4 of 4, and the last stage, of the `/manage` decomposition (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-manage-slash-decomposition-design.md`): every DB-mutating operation function `handlers/manage/*.js`'s stage-2 split produced now calls `utils/changeStore.js`'s `recordChange()` once, right after its own save succeeds — the hook point that split existed to create in the first place.

**`models/ChangeLog.js` + `utils/changeStore.js`** copy the `/alerts` trio's shape (`models/AlertLog.js` / `utils/alertStore.js` / `commands/alerts.js`) directly, since that pattern already solves human-referenceable ids, read-back pagination, export and retention: a `changeId` (`MmmDD-NN`) allocated race-free through the existing `AlertCounter` `$inc` upsert, namespaced under a `chg-` key so the two logs' daily counters never collide; `recordChange()` is fire-and-forget and never-throwing, same contract as `recordAlert()`, so a logging failure can never break the admin action that triggered it; retention at 180 days or 5,000 rows, throttled hourly.

**`commands/audit.js` + `handlers/audit.js`** are `/alerts`' shape rebuilt for this log: summary tiles, a paginated list with the page number encoded statelessly in the customId, export to a `.txt` attachment, and filters by page and by actor (a select-menu dropdown for the page filter, a one-field modal for the actor filter — both ride along in every subsequent customId so the pager, export and clear-filters buttons all respect whatever's active). Harkirat chose this shape over the design spec's own recommendation, which was an "Audit Log" page inside `/manage` — he picked a separate command mirroring `/alerts` instead. `setIntegrationTypes([1])` (stays user-install-only like every other admin command), gated by its own `'audit'` token in `utils/adminAccess.js`, and added to `bot/registry.js`'s `ADMIN_COMMAND_NAMES` so `/admin` can never gate it.

**Every hook was checked against the real operation-function signatures rather than the handoff's table taken on faith** — `purgeDraws(scope)`/`deleteDraw(match)` (draws), `calendar.purge()`/`deleteItem(match)`, `patchnotes.purge()`, and `loadouts.deleteItem(match)` had no `interaction` in scope at all (they're called from `handlers/manage/index.js`'s `PURGE_HANDLERS`/`DELETE_HANDLERS` maps with only a `scope`/`match`), so each gained an `actorId` parameter threaded through from `index.js`'s dispatch, which already has `interaction.user.id` in hand at the call site. Every other operation function already had `interaction` directly.

🔴 **`ChangeLog.actorId` is a per-user Discord ID, so `docs/legal/PRIVACY.md` was updated in the same change** (§2.1b + Appendix A, version bumped) — `npm run docs:audit`'s `privacy-model-coverage` check exists specifically to catch a new model gaining a per-user field, and now also matches `actorId` itself (widened from its existing `discordId`/`userId`/`updatedBy`/`createdBy`/`authorId`/`ownerId` set) so this model can never silently drift undisclosed. `dior legal build` ran and `public/` is committed alongside it — unlike a changelog/DEVLOG-only change, which never needs that.

**Verification.** `scripts/changeStore.test.js` (new, wired into `npm test`) mutation-validates `recordChange()`'s never-throwing contract and `pruneChanges()`'s throttle, each proven to fail when the guarded behaviour is broken. Full `npm test` green, `docs:audit` at zero errors including `privacy-inventory` and `privacy-model-coverage`. Live click-test on the dev bot — a real `/manage` edit followed by `/audit` showing the row with the right actor/page/action/target, pagination, export, and an Undo flipping the row's `undone` flag — is deferred to a session where Harkirat can drive it, same as stages 1–3's click-testing (`docs/db-deferred-list.md`'s LIVE CLICK-TEST OWED entry covers this too).

This closes the four-stage `/manage` decomposition project: `docs/db-deferred-list.md`'s Queued entry for it moves to `docs/archive/resolved-list.md` in this same change.

## Pre-Release v3.23.0 — 2026-08-15 12:07 EDT (#131 · `403d50d`) — Bulk-cache pipeline for the nameplate/decoration catalog

Pre-renders the 925-SKU catalog into the bot's existing Cloudinary + Discord storage-channel cache, replacing the lazy per-user-equip discovery path for anything catalogued (the lazy path stays as the fallback for anything not yet catalogued).

- **`models/CollectibleCatalog.js` + `scripts/syncCatalogToMongo.js`** — a Mongo mirror of the catalog JSON, one doc per SKU, additive sync that never resets bulk-cache progress on re-run.
- **`scripts/bulkCacheCollectibles.js`** — grouped by design so a multi-variant design posts as ONE cache-channel message (dividers between variants) instead of one per SKU, with expanded metadata (description, parent category, variant colors) and a `render_source: 'catalog'|'fallback'` marker that lets a live-user render from before the catalog existed be found and healed automatically. Nameplate variants use the original full-width Media Gallery + metadata layout; decorations keep Section+Thumbnail.
- **Nameplate render pivoted** from the old slug-based webm/`libvpx-vp9` route to the same SKU-addressed `/animated` APNG endpoint decorations already used, dropping that decoder workaround entirely. Both cache modules split into a shared render core plus separate single-item/bulk upload paths so the live and bulk pipelines can't drift apart.
- Verified live against the dev bot: a fresh apng render end-to-end, real multi-variant grouped messages up to 7 variants, fallback-to-catalog healing, and a 150-group/169-SKU batching stress run with zero failures.
- The full run against **prod** is a v3 pre-launch item, not part of this release — the prod bot currently has no access to the dedicated storage server, and fixing that requires enabling guild-install for the prod app, which is deliberately bundled with v3's own public guild-install launch rather than done early.

## Pre-Release v3.22.0 — 2026-08-15 01:50 EDT (#130 · `8ecfad6`) — The full nameplate/decoration catalog lands, with a script to keep it synced

Harkirat hand-authored a complete snapshot of Discord's entire nameplate + decoration collectibles catalog and dropped it into the repo. This entry tracks getting it into shape as tracked, documented reference data, plus the tooling to refresh it going forward — no bot runtime code changed.

**`docs/reference/nameplate-decoration-catalog.json`** (renamed from `all-nameplates-decorations.json`) — 88 collections, 235 nameplate design groups (262 SKUs), 490 decoration design groups (663 SKUs), 925 SKUs total, 0 duplicates, verified by parsing the file programmatically rather than sampling it. Tracked in git deliberately (not `local/`) specifically so a future refresh produces a real diff of what Discord added. A companion **`docs/reference/nameplate-decoration-catalog.md`** documents the schema, the `palette_hex` (bed color) vs. `variant_value` (art colorway) distinction, the display-name rule (`"<group_name> (<variant_label>)"`), and the SKU-addressed asset-fetch URLs (`/animated` returns a real multi-frame APNG, unlike the slug-based route this codebase already uses elsewhere).

**`scripts/syncNameplateCatalog.py`** — the repo's first Python script. Fetches Discord's live `collectibles-categories/v2` endpoint and additively merges anything genuinely new into the catalog file; existing entries are never rewritten, and a run that finds nothing new leaves the file byte-identical (field order was matched to the existing file's exact convention for this reason). **Requires a Discord user token, not a bot token** — live-verified on both `api/v9` and `api/v10` that a bot token gets a hard `403 {"code": 20001, "message": "Bots cannot use this endpoint"}`; no bot-token path exists. Because a user token calling this private client API to automate fetches is Discord's definition of self-botting, the script is **deliberately run manually only — no cron, no launchd** (Harkirat's call, so it never becomes standing account automation). Credentials live in the gitignored `scripts/.env.discord-sync`.

**Filed, not built this round:** a bulk pre-cache of the full catalog into the existing Cloudinary/Discord-storage-channel pipeline, and whether the catalog itself should move to a Mongoose collection once that pipeline exists. Both need Harkirat's sign-off — see `docs/db-deferred-list.md`'s re-scoped nameplate/decoration item.

**Verification.** `docs:audit` (40/41 verified, 1 correctly skipped — no `--diff`) and `docs:reflow --check` (51 files, 0 would change) both pass. `syncNameplateCatalog.py` run live end-to-end (`--dry-run` and a real run) against Harkirat's actual credentials — correctly found 0 new SKUs and left the file untouched.

## Pre-Release v3.21.0 — 2026-08-14 18:09 EDT (#129 · `0ddfa97`) — `/manage data_for:draws action:add-new` opens the modal directly

Stage 3 of the four-stage `/manage` decomposition (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-manage-slash-decomposition-design.md`): a new `action` string option on `/manage`, scoped autocomplete, and a dispatch branch in `execute()` that resolves and runs a page's own action without ever rendering the panel — the original ask this whole decomposition existed to reach.

**The option can't use static `choices()`** — Discord has no way to scope one option's choices by another option's live value, and a flat list would be ~40 entries against the 25-choice cap while also offering Loadout actions on the Calendar page. So `action` is autocomplete, and `handlers/router.js` gained a scoped route: it reads `data_for`, rejects anyone `hasCommandAccess`/`getManagePages` wouldn't already let see that page (an autocomplete interaction carries no `customId`, so the router's prefix guard doesn't cover it — this route re-implements the same check `execute()` opens with), then filters `listSlashActions(page)` through the same `fuzzyMatch` every other autocomplete route in the bot uses.

**The design spec's dispatch plan didn't survive contact with the code it was dispatching to.** It called for deferring before running `kind: 'file'`/`'view'` actions and skipping the defer only for `'modal'`. Reading the actual `run()` implementations in `utils/manageActions.js` before wiring this up showed that's already wrong today: `exportFile()` calls `interaction.reply()` directly (a `deferReply()` first would throw "already acknowledged"), and `openFormatGuide()` (`'view'`) already defers itself. Every `run()` fully owns its own response mode — that's the entire point of the registry's `kind` field. So `execute()`'s new branch does exactly what the button dispatch in `handlers/manage/index.js` already does: resolve, then call `run()` with no defer of its own, full stop. An unresolvable or unpermitted `action` falls through to a normal page render with a short note prepended, rather than failing the whole invocation over a typo.

**A completeness sweep caught a real gap in this same feature before it shipped: `resolveAction()` never checked `slash`, so a `slash:false` destructive action (purge/wipe/promote/discard) was reachable by typing its id directly** — `/manage data_for:draws action:purgeall` would have opened the confirm prompt via the new dispatch, even though autocomplete never suggests those ids. Autocomplete suggestions aren't server-enforced by Discord, so "not suggested" isn't "rejected". Fixed by adding the `resolved.entry.slash` check in `execute()`'s dispatch branch, the one place that needs it, since `resolveAction()` is shared with the button path where a button's `custom_id` can only ever be one a page actually rendered. Pinned by a new source-scan test proven to fail on the exact reverted line.

**Boot-testing this on the dev bot surfaced an unrelated, severe, bot-wide bug that was blocking the verification itself — fixed in the same change.** `handlers/colors.js`'s `handleColorsButton` was the only one of the thirteen per-subsystem handlers with no `customId` presence check; every other one opens with `if (!ownsCustomId(interaction.customId)) return false;`, whose helper checks `typeof customId === 'string'` first. Colours sits last in `handlers/router.js`'s dispatch chain, so **any interaction with no `customId` — meaning any plain slash-command invocation, or any autocomplete interaction, for any command in the bot — crashed there unconditionally** the moment it reached that point, ever since colours was the first handler extracted (2026-08-13 16:45 EDT) — before the type-test convention itself was even established (found later that same day at 18:45 EDT and applied to the other twelve handlers, never backported here). The crash net logged it and returned, so the interaction was simply never acknowledged. Fixed with the same one-line guard the other twelve already carry, deliberately just a presence check rather than gating on `OWNED_PREFIXES` — that would change this module's own documented contract of letting an unrecognised `colors_*` id fall through.

**Verification.** Full `npm test` green (15/15 registry checks including two new ones for the option's autocomplete flag and `listSlashActions()`'s per-page filtering, `docs:reflow`, 26/26 hook self-tests), `docs:audit` at 40/41 verified + 1 correctly skipped (the diff-only conservation check), 0 errors. Dev bot boots clean and stays clean over a 40s window post-fix (crashed within seconds pre-fix on a real stray interaction, which is how this was caught). Live click-test of the `action:` slash surface itself is still pending (deferred, same as stages 1–2, to a session where Harkirat can drive it) — this session has no Discord client access to trigger one directly.

## Pre-Release v3.20.0 — 2026-08-14 17:24 EDT (#128 · `8e3183a`) — `/manage` stops being one 2,416-line file

Stage 2 of the four-stage `/manage` decomposition (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-manage-slash-decomposition-design.md`): the single `routeManage()` dispatcher, at 56% of the whole interaction router on its own, becomes a directory — `handlers/manage/index.js` (a thin, prefix-matched dispatcher) plus `shared.js` (the cross-page helpers, the pending-confirmation token maps, and a new `prompt()` render helper) plus one module per page (`draws.js`, `calendar.js`, `loadouts.js`, `patchnotes.js`, `season.js`, `admins.js`, `announcements.js`). Every branch's behavior is unchanged — this is a move, not a rewrite — with one deliberate exception.

**All ~25 confirm/cancel/undo prompts now render through `sendV2Payload` instead of a raw `interaction.update()` call.** That legacy shape was the one documented gap in v3.17.0's bot-wide passive-expiry rollout: those prompts never got their own idle-disable timer, and `handlers/router.js` compensated with a narrow safety net that cancelled — never rescheduled — any pending timer before dispatching into `/manage`, so a stale timer could never overwrite a confirm prompt with an earlier page's components. The new `prompt(interaction, {text, components})` helper wraps the same content in a single Text Display and calls straight into `sendV2Payload`, which already performs the identical Discord operation (a `type: 7` UPDATE_MESSAGE) for an un-acked interaction — so the swap is behaviorally a no-op that also closes the gap. **The router's safety net is not deleted yet.** The design doc's own instruction was to verify the swap on the dev bot before removing it, and that live click-test — the one thing a CLI session can't do for itself — is deferred to a session where Harkirat is available to click through the panel; until then the net is provably harmless (a cancelled timer gets rescheduled a moment later by the new V2 render) rather than load-bearing, so it stays.

**The ~45 scattered DB-write call sites collapsed into named per-page operation functions** — `purgeDraws(scope)`, `deleteDraw(match)`, `bulkAddOrReplaceCalendar`, `setDateInfo`, `editLoadout`, and so on — which is the hook stage 4's audit log needs and did not have before: there was no single place to call a `recordChange()` once per mutation.

**Version note:** this lands as v3.20.0-pre rather than the v3.19.0-pre the design doc named, because an unrelated PR (#127, this same changelog's previous entry) merged in between and consumed that number first.

**Verification.** Full `npm test` green — the routing-contract suite (`scripts/handlerRouting.test.js`) needed five of its ten checks made directory-aware, since they previously assumed one file per handler module; a stateful per-line scan (the intra-module shadow detector) now resets at each physical file boundary instead of leaking state across a directory's files. The 57-action registry harness, the state/concurrency tests, `docs:reflow`, and all 26 hook self-tests are unaffected and green. The dev bot boots clean under the new layout (Mongo connects, gateway authenticates, no errors) — confirming the module wiring at runtime, not just `node --check`. A conservation pass diffed every code-level string literal in the deleted file against the new files via git; it caught one paraphrased comment losing a specific detail (a Mongo index name in a debugging note), now restored. **Not yet click-tested live in Discord** — deferred, per Harkirat, to a session where he can drive the panel.

## Pre-Release v3.19.0 — 2026-08-14 16:27 EDT (#127 · `b319c8a`) — A presence check for the memory layer, and an expiring hook stopped asserting its own reversal

Two failures, found the same day, both invisible from inside a session. `sequential-thinking`'s JSON-Schema dialect fix (2026-08-13) had landed in the Claude **Desktop** config, not `~/.claude.json`, so no Claude Code session ever saw it — the shim was real and correct, just on the wrong client. `perseus-vault` was worse: it sat at "⏸ Pending approval," a state only an interactive `claude` run can clear and that no session can detect, so `memory-write-gate` nagged about writes that were never possible to make.

**`.claude/hooks/mcp-layer-check.sh` now checks server presence by name every session** — it warns, with the exact `claude mcp add --scope user` fix command, when an expected server is missing from Claude Code's config, and separately when a server is configured for Desktop but never mirrored to Code. A second, unrelated bug in the same hook was fixed in the same pass: its `sequential-thinking` observation-window block had auto-expired on 2026-08-09 and then spent five days injecting the opposite of what Harkirat had decided that same day, with data. An auto-expiring guard must expire into silence or a question, never a claim about a decision it cannot know happened — replaced with the standing verdict, plus an assertion that makes restoring the retired rule a test failure.

All five local servers (`linksee`, `perseus-vault`, `sequential-thinking`, `codebase-memory-mcp`, `jina-reader`) now report ✔ Connected in a real session. This branch also carried a full MCP connector and plugin audit once the parity gap was closed — three hard-failing plugins disabled, `mongodb`/`cloudinary` enabled, Cloudinary's connector surface trimmed from six overlapping entries to two after discovering the apparent "duplicate" pair actually differed by credential storage. None of it touches bot code; full record in `local/handoff/2026-08-14-mcp-connector-audit.md`.

**Verification.** `npm run test:hooks` green (26 hooks, 10 new mutation-validated cases for this fix), `docs:audit` at 0 errors.

## Pre-Release v3.18.0 — 2026-08-14 13:45 EDT (#126) — `/manage`'s actions become one table instead of two copies of the same list

Stage 1 of four in the `/manage` decomposition designed this session (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-manage-slash-decomposition-design.md`): a single action registry, then a per-page handler split, then the scoped `action:` slash option, then a DB-change audit log behind a new `/audit` command. This release is the first of those and changes nothing a user can see — every button renders with the same label, opens the same modal, and writes the same data as before.

**The action list existed twice, and nothing compared the two copies.** `commands/manage.js`'s `buildPagesTable()` held one — the `{ id, label, style }` button rows on every page — and `handlers/manage.js`'s `mng_act_` branch held the other, a 220-line `if/else` naming the same ids again to decide what each does. Keeping them in step was manual, and both ways of failing were silent: a button whose id no handler matches renders normally and does nothing at all when clicked, and a handler whose button was removed is dead code that still reads as a supported feature. The upcoming `action:` slash option would have made a third copy of the same list, in a file that had already reached 2,608 lines with a single 2,311-line function inside it.

**`utils/manageActions.js` is now the one place an action is described** — its label, its button style, what it does, and which page's permission it needs — and both call sites read from it. `buildPagesTable()` keeps only the ids each group offers (`buttons: ['addnew', 'edit', 'delete']`), with `buttonFor()` resolving the label and style at render time; the `mng_act_` branch parses the custom_id, resolves the entry, and runs it. That branch went from 222 lines to 30, and `handlers/manage.js` from 2,608 to 2,416.

**Per-page admin permissions became per-CLICK for every panel BUTTON in the same move, closing half of a gap filed 2026-08-13.** They were previously checked only when a page was opened, which meant a panel message left sitting in a channel kept working after its clicker's access had been narrowed. Every action now resolves through one function that checks the entry's own page scope, so the check happens where the click does. `handlers/router.js`'s prefix guard still runs first and independently — that one answers "may this user touch `/manage` at all", the new one answers "may they touch THIS page" — and both are required. **The other half of that gap is explicitly still open and was re-filed rather than quietly absorbed:** modal submits (`modal_calendar_bulk_add` and its siblings) do not pass through the resolver, because their custom_ids encode their page inconsistently and there is no single extraction that works. Stage 2 moves each modal branch into a module that knows its own page by construction, which is where that check belongs; doing it now would mean writing a per-handler version and then deleting it.

**Two fields on each entry are load-bearing rather than descriptive, and both are documented as such where someone editing the table will see them.** `kind` (`'modal'` / `'file'` / `'confirm'` / `'view'`) exists because Discord requires `showModal()` to be an interaction's first response and it cannot follow `deferReply()` — declaring the response mode per action lets a caller decide whether it may defer *before* it does, instead of every new action rediscovering that rule the hard way. `slash` marks whether the stage-3 `action:` option may open that action directly, and is written out per entry rather than derived from `kind` on purpose: the rule it enforces (destructive actions stay panel-only, so reaching one always costs a deliberate navigation) happens to be exactly "every `kind: 'confirm'`" today, and deriving the flag would make the test that enforces it vacuously true.

**Verification.** `scripts/manageActions.test.js` (12 checks, wired into `npm test`) asserts conservation in both directions — every rendered button resolves to a registered action, and every registered action is reachable from a button — plus that no destructive action is slash-exposed, that every purge action has the confirmation label it reads at click time, and that the MP and DMZ loadout pages offer identical sets. It was mutation-validated rather than assumed: four seeded breakages (a button removed from the page table, an unregistered id added to it, a destructive action marked slash-exposed, a purge label deleted) were each caught by a different check, and the baseline returned green after every revert. Separately, all 57 registered actions were invoked against the local dev database with a stubbed interaction, confirming each reaches the right Discord call with the right modal, filename, or confirm-button custom_ids. **And the panel was diffed against itself across the change**: the same script rendered every page at `e3d1a88` and at HEAD and dumped all 57 buttons — page, custom_id, style and label — with **zero difference**. That is the check the conservation tests structurally cannot make, since they prove the two remaining copies agree rather than that either still matches what shipped, and 57 labels and styles were hand-transcribed out of the old page table. The bot boots clean on the dev token. **Not yet click-tested live in Discord** — that is owed before stage 2 builds on top of this.

## Pre-Release v3.17.0 — 2026-08-14 11:14 EDT (#125 · `e3d1a88`) — the idle-disable timer stops being a `/settings` exclusive, and `/server` becomes `/admin`

Two independent pieces of work, done together at Harkirat's request in one session: extend the passive 10-minute idle-disable mechanism bot-wide, and rename `/server` to `/admin` — *"feels more intuitive for the server admin users."* A third item, decomposing `/manage` into dedicated slash-driven actions, was scoped for the same session and explicitly deferred to its own — see `docs/db-deferred-list.md`'s Queued entry for the live version of that idea.

**Passive expiry generalized from one command to the whole bot, by moving where it lives rather than copying it.** `/settings` shipped this mechanism alone back in v2.22.0: every render schedules a `setTimeout`, holding that render's own fresh interaction token, that PATCHes the message's components to `disabled: true` after 10 idle minutes, with any later interaction on the message cancelling and rescheduling — a genuine sliding window, not a fixed deadline. Extending it to every other command was filed as an open roadmap item ever since, because the naive version — an explicit `schedulePanelExpiry` call at every command's own send site — would have meant editing a dozen-plus files and staying correct at every future one too. Instead the scheduling call moved into `utils/sendV2Payload.js` itself, the shared V2 send/patch boundary nearly every panel in the bot already funnels through: any render containing at least one enabled button or select now schedules or reschedules its own timer automatically, with no per-command code. That includes every command whose pagination/nav buttons re-render by replaying the originating command's own `execute()` through a synthetic interaction (`utils/interactionContext.js`) — the replay calls `sendV2Payload` again on its own, so those re-renders reschedule for free too. `commands/settings.js`'s original explicit call was removed as redundant; nothing about its behavior changed, only where the call now lives.

**The message id comes from two different places depending on which render this is, and getting that wrong would have silently broken the light/single-hop pagination path.** A component-triggered re-render already carries `interaction.message.id` — reliable regardless of whether the response ends up going through the deferred `PATCH .../@original` path or the undeferred single-hop `POST .../callback` path added by the pagination perf work (which returns Discord's bare 204, no body, for exactly this case). Only the very first render of a fresh slash command has no `.message` yet, so that one case reads the id off the `PATCH` response instead — the same value `/settings` was already relying on. `scripts/passiveExpiry.test.js` (18 cases, wired into `npm test`) pins both paths and the "nothing to disable" no-op case, verified non-vacuous by mutation: temporarily disabling the two scheduling calls flips exactly the three tests that assert on them and nothing else.

**One subsystem, `/manage`, gets a narrower, explicitly documented treatment instead of full instrumentation.** Its confirm/cancel/undo micro-prompts — roughly two dozen call sites inside `handlers/manage.js`'s 2,608-line `routeManage()` — edit the panel message via discord.js's raw `interaction.update()` rather than `sendV2Payload`, because they're plain content+button messages, not a Components V2 container. Hand-touching every one of those call sites under this session's time budget was judged a worse trade than the alternative: `handlers/router.js` now cancels — never reschedules — any pending timer for the message the instant a `/manage`-owned interaction lands, before dispatching into the panel. Without it, a timer armed by an earlier `sendV2Payload`-based page render could still be pending when a raw-update confirm prompt replaces it on screen, and if 10 minutes then passed with the user staring at that prompt, the stale timer would fire and PATCH the message back to the *earlier* page's components — just disabled, and visibly wrong. Cancelling outright closes that; the accepted cost is narrower and more honest: one of those short-lived prompts runs with no countdown of its own until the next real page render re-arms one. Filed as a named follow-up bundled with the (deferred) `/manage` decomposition session, since that work is rebuilding this file's interaction model anyway.

**`commands/admin.js`'s own re-renders were switched from raw `interaction.update()` to `sendV2Payload` for the same two reasons at once.** It's the pattern every other V2 panel in the bot already uses (root `CLAUDE.md`'s "V2 sends" rule: discord.js's high-level reply/followUp/update don't reliably serialize raw Components V2 JSON), and it's what makes the panel pick up the new idle-disable for free. The extra weight behind doing this now rather than leaving it: this command had never been real-world click-tested live — `docs/ROADMAP.md`'s own click-test checklist named it the one deliberate holdout — so matching the battle-tested send path is strictly safer regardless of whether the raw call happened to actually work.

**`/server` is `/admin` now — command name, every custom_id prefix, the source file, its rule file, and every live cross-reference, renamed together in one pass.** `server_*` custom_ids became `admin_*`, `commands/server.js` became `commands/admin.js`, `.claude/rules/server-controls.md` became `admin-controls.md`, and the rename reached `CLAUDE.md`'s nav map, `docs/legal/PRIVACY.md`'s pending-v3 §2.1a description (the command didn't exist under its new name yet when that section was written, so it now correctly describes what actually ships), `docs/README.md`'s rules list, and both routing test suites. `isServerAdmin()` and the `serverAdmin` permission-check key were deliberately left alone — they name the *concept* (an admin of a Discord server), not this specific command, the same distinction that already applies to `/manage`'s unrelated owner-level panel. The panel's own heading changed from "Server Controls" to "Server Admin", and its `/help` landing-directory tag changed from `(Admin)` to `(server)`, per Harkirat's follow-up in the same session — along with a handful of leftover `/server` mentions the first rename pass missed in code comments (`bot/registry.js`, `handlers/router.js`, `scripts/guildPolicy.test.js`).

**Verification, this release:** `node --check` on every touched file, the full `npm test` chain (every subsystem test, `docs:reflow`, and all 26 hook self-tests) green, `docs:audit` at 0 errors. Not yet click-tested live in Discord under the new name — `/server` itself was already the one deliberate click-test holdout from v3.16.0 onward, and that status carries over to `/admin`.

## Pre-Release v3.16.0 — 2026-08-13 17:28 EDT (#124 · `7ef5004`) — index.js stops being a code dump and becomes an entrypoint

**`index.js` went from 4,553 lines to 129, and the interaction router that came out of it went from 3,684 to ~470.** It had become a single file holding the bot's boot sequence, its command registration, its lifecycle listeners and a ~3,400-line `interactionCreate` handler that was really a giant custom_id switch. The split was already a launch-blocking v3 item, and the ordering mattered: this refactor rewrites the exact router the v3 launch click-test exercises, so doing it afterwards would have meant testing code that no longer existed.

It landed in two passes, deliberately — the first proved the pattern on one subsystem, the second used it on the whole router.

**Pass one — one subsystem, chosen by measurement.** The five `colors_*` button branches came to 382 contiguous lines touching neither `client` nor `client.commands`, with every branch terminating and a 10s refresh cooldown used nowhere else. Draw prices, the other candidate, was 60 lines but needed `client.commands.get('draw')` — which would have put a client dependency into the very first handler's contract. `handlers/colors.js` was the result, along with `utils/interactionContext.js` holding `buildSyntheticInteraction` and `resolvePanelActor`, **moved rather than copied**: the first of those encodes the fix for two real past crashes, and a second copy that drifted would have quietly reintroduced them.

**Pass two — the whole dispatcher.** `handlers/router.js` now holds the `interactionCreate` handler and the router-private helpers and short-lived stores that only it ever touched (the `/manage` undo and pending-confirmation Maps, its id parsing and search resolution, the bulk upsert helpers, the anti-spam cooldown). Their privacy was verified against every use site first, not assumed. `index.js` registers the router as a plain listener.

**Pass three — the boot sequence.** `bot/registry.js` owns which commands exist and pushing them to Discord, in three stages kept separate because they run at different times: on-disk modules (synchronous, at boot), the DB-derived per-category weapon commands (async, post-ready — they cannot be built at require time), then one REST PUT. `bot/lifecycle.js` owns every client listener that is not routing: the `error` net, the five shard diagnostics, ClientReady, restart labeling, the daily heartbeat, the Cloudinary cleanup — registered in their original order. `index.js` is left with connect, construct, wire, log in.

Both new modules sit one level below the repo root, which moved two `__dirname`-relative paths: the `commands/` scan and the `.restart-reason` marker, now anchored against `..`. Both fail *silently* if wrong — an empty command set, or every deploy mislabeled as an unattended restart — so both carry a comment saying exactly that.

**The three risks the roadmap named were designed around, not discovered afterwards.** The crash net travelled *with* the handler — the single top-level try/catch still wraps every branch, and `index.js` still registers `client.on('error', …)` beside it, because `captureRejections` means neither covers the other. Routing order is untouched: the `/manage` per-page admin guard and the `/server` dispatcher still run first. And the extracted handler returns `true`/`false` rather than the router blanket-matching a `colors_` prefix, so an unrecognised `colors_*` id still falls through exactly as it did — pinned by a routing-contract test — written colours-only in this pass, then generalised in pass four into `scripts/handlerRouting.test.js` once there were thirteen handlers to hold to the same contract. Its sharpest case survived the generalisation: `colors_subpage_indicator`, the paginator's own disabled button, is colours-prefixed and must **not** be consumed.

**`client` is deliberately not imported by the router.** All 19 `client.commands` reads became `interaction.client.commands` — the same Collection, reached through the interaction already in hand, which is what lets the router be a pure module instead of depending on the entrypoint that requires it.

Five now-dead imports were dropped from `index.js` in the process (`renderTiming`, `resolveThumbnail`, and the three above). A pre-existing `docs:audit` `nav-map-sync` failure was fixed in passing: `admin-access-and-announcements.md` shipped with #123 without being added to either index.

**Pass four — the router gives up everything that belongs to a subsystem.** Thirteen modules now live in `handlers/`: `manage` (2,608 lines on its own — 56% of the old router), plus `settings`, `loadouts`, `autobuild`, `drawprices`, `navigation`, `pagination`, `share`, `alerts`, `timestamp`, `help`, `patchnotes` and the original `colors`. `handlers/router.js` is down to ~470 lines and holds only what belongs to nobody: the ordered guard stack, the dispatch chain, and the two routes that are not custom_id-shaped — autocomplete and the slash-command engine. The three `isStringSelectMenu()` / `isButton()` / `isModalSubmit()` blocks are gone entirely.

**Ownership is decided by custom_id prefix, before any branch body runs, and that is what made a move this size safe.** Every subsystem's prefixes were checked to be mutually exclusive at extraction time, so deciding ownership up front cannot change which handler wins — which in turn meant **not one `return` statement had to be rewritten**. Rewriting ~100 returns across `/manage` to satisfy a boolean contract is exactly how a refactor this size plants a bug on one rarely-clicked confirmation button. `scripts/handlerRouting.test.js` now makes prefix exclusivity a permanent test rather than a one-time check: it fails if any two modules claim overlapping prefixes, because two owners means the first in the chain silently swallows the other's clicks. Proven to fail — injecting a `nav_` collision into `alerts` reports it and exits 1.

**The ~100 cross-references were updated too, and how that went is the more useful record.** Comments across `commands/`, `utils/`, `scripts/`, `handlers/`, `docs/reference/` and the rule files addressed the handlers as "`index.js`'s X handler". The first attempt was a script mapping each mention to a module via the custom_id prefix on the same line; it rewrote 49 and got a meaningful share wrong — a handler header citing its own file, autocomplete attributed to the wrong module, paths mangled mid-sentence inside rule files. **It was reverted wholesale, because a wrong reference costs more than a stale one**: it sends a reader to a file that genuinely does not contain the thing. What worked was listing every match, deciding each target by hand against the new prefix→module table, and applying them as explicit `from → to` pairs that fail loudly on a mismatch — 100 replacements across 40 files, zero misses. Seven mentions of `index.js` survive on purpose and are correct: the `unhandledRejection`/`uncaughtException` nets really are still in the entrypoint, and two more are historical "used to live here" notes.

`.claude/rules/interaction-router.md` is now canonical for all of this — the file layout, the handler contract, the prefix→module table, and the note on which surviving `index.js` mentions are deliberate.

**One real bug shipped in the split and was caught before merge — by asking what the MOVED COMMENTS still asserted.** Several relocated comments referenced "the `isButton()` block" and "the `isStringSelectMenu()` block above", blocks the split had deleted. `manage.js` turned out to reproduce all three, so its comments still resolved. The generated modules did not — and that mattered, because the type blocks had been doing real work. **`set_page_` (a button) also matches `startsWith('set_')` (a select branch)**, so a `/settings` page-navigation click entered the select handler, deferred, then threw on `interaction.values[0]`; buttons have no `.values`. The router's crash net swallowed it, so the button just looked dead. `loadouts.js` had the same shape latent — `mpbrowse` also matches the pagination branch's `startsWith('mp')` — and worked only because the exact-match branch happened to sit first.

Fixed by making the type test explicit in every branch of a mixed-type handler, and `scripts/handlerRouting.test.js` now enforces it two ways: it drives a *button* at `set_page_2` and `mpbrowse` through a mock whose `values` getter throws, and it scans the source so an untyped branch in a mixed-type module fails outright. Both were verified to fail when the guard is removed. **The general lesson is the uncomfortable one:** every branch body was preserved byte-for-byte and behaviour still broke, because what was lost lived in the structure *around* the code. Byte-identity is not behaviour-identity.

**Two more gaps came out of a wider sweep after the branch was pushed, and both were invisible to every gate.** First, **the subsystem rule files stopped routing to the code**: `.claude/rules/*.md` load by path glob, and those globs still pointed only at `commands/*.js` — so editing `handlers/manage.js`, which holds 2,608 lines of `/manage` logic, no longer loaded the `/manage` panel rule. The deepest subsystem knowledge silently stopped reaching the file that now contains the subsystem. Eight rule files gained the handler paths they describe. `rule-globs` could not catch this: every glob it checked still matched a real file, and it has no way to know a *different* file should also be covered.

Second, **the routing test had a blind spot in exactly the check that protects the design**. `colors.js` never declared its prefixes, so the exclusivity scan carried a hardcoded `['colors_']` — meaning a new colours prefix would have been invisible to the one test that stops two handlers claiming the same id. Every handler now declares `OWNED_PREFIXES` (`manage.js`'s differently-named export was unified), the hardcoded list is gone, and a handler that fails to declare now fails the test rather than quietly contributing nothing. Verified by removing the declaration and watching it fail.

**The strongest check was the last one run, and it came from asking what KIND of check had never happened.** Everything up to that point compared text, counted sets, or exercised one path. What none of it asked was: *for every custom_id, does the new code select the same branch the old code would have?* Simulating both routers over the id corpus — each id carried with the interaction type the old code gated it behind — gives **92/92 identical routing decisions**. And it is not a ritual: re-run against the code exactly as it was when first pushed, it reports `set_page_ [isButton] old → set_page_, new → set_`, i.e. **it would have caught the type-guard bug before it ever shipped**.

The differential itself is a migration check and dies with the migration, but its ongoing half became permanent: `handlerRouting.test.js` now also asserts **no branch is shadowed by an earlier branch in the same module** — the general form of the specific bug, since a shadowed branch is dead code that looks live. Three independent checks now catch that class (a runtime probe, a type-test scan, and shadowing), and all three were verified to fail when the guard is removed.

**The comments moved with the code, and two kinds of them stopped being true — neither detectable by searching for a filename.** Harkirat asked directly whether the context comments beside each moved element were now stale, and they were, in ways every earlier sweep was blind to because none of them mentions `index.js` at all.

**The numbering and lettering schemes are gone entirely — now a standing convention.** `index.js` organised itself with `PHASE 2`…`PHASE 6`, `STEP 6.1`…`6.5`, `ADMIN ROUTE A`…`K`, and per-handler letters `A.`–`K.` Harkirat's call once the first batch surfaced: *"ditch the numbering/lettering system and just do section headers. as code changes, the numbering/lettering go stale."*

He is right, and the split had already demonstrated it four ways at once. `index.js` and `bot/registry.js` both ended up with a **`PHASE 4`** meaning different things, and `PHASE 5` was both "LOGIN" and "CLIENT LIFECYCLE" — collisions I introduced myself while splitting. **`A.`, `C.` and `F.` each labelled two unrelated sections** in different files. `colors.js` carried **`B.6`–`B.8`** while its implied siblings `B.1`–`B.5` sat in `settings.js` and `pagination.js`, so a reader looking for them finds nothing. And `router.js` kept **`STEP 6.1`/`6.2`** after 6.3–6.5 were deleted, leaving holes — while two `index.js` breadcrumbs existed *solely* to explain earlier gaps in that same numbering, one of them pointing at a note that no longer existed. Removing the scheme removed the need for both.

**44 labels stripped to plain descriptive headers**; the comments that cross-referenced them by letter now cite the **custom_id**, which is greppable and cannot drift. A label encodes position; a description says what the code *is*. Enforced across `index.js`, `bot/` and `handlers/` by `scripts/handlerRouting.test.js`, with ordered lists inside a paragraph deliberately not matched.

**Positional language pointing across a file boundary.** A comment saying a handler is "further down" was true in a 4,553-line file and is a lie once that handler lives elsewhere. Four such cases: `drawprices.js` describing the `toggle_` handler as "further down" when it is in `settings.js`, and `settings.js` citing `calpage_`/`price_region_`/`price_subpage_` as "above" when they are in `pagination.js` and `drawprices.js`. Both now name the owning file. This is invisible to every other check in the suite — the code is correct and only the prose is wrong, which is precisely what the next person navigates by — so it is now check 7 in `handlerRouting.test.js`, flagging a positional reference to a foreign-owned custom_id unless the line names that module's file. Naming the file is both the fix and the escape hatch. Verified falsifiable.

**Checked structurally, not by eye:** 93 `custom_id` branches existed before the split and 93 exist after, none lost or gained · all 171 relative `require` paths in the new and changed files resolve · every new module loads under Node · the dev bot booted clean after each pass, reaching both `handleBotReady()` lines. `docs:audit` was genuinely RED for the new `bot/` directory until CLAUDE.md gained a runtime-layout section — an earlier `tail -4` had hidden that failure behind the summary line, which is its own lesson about reading a gate's exit code rather than its last four lines.

**A later audit asked what KIND of check had still never run, and the most useful answer was a question about copies.** Everything up to that point examined the new tree for internal consistency or compared it against the old one. Nothing asked *who else holds a copy of a list this refactor moved* — and extraction creates duplicates wherever the original is still needed in place. It had: `router.js`'s `MANAGE_PREFIX_COMMAND`, the choke point deciding who may click a `/manage`, `/autobuild` or `/alerts` component, carries its own copy of those three modules' prefixes, because it maps each to a **command name** for the per-command permission lookup that `OWNED_PREFIXES` does not encode. The two lists are byte-identical and nothing checked that they stay so. Add `mng_newthing` to `handlers/manage.js`, forget the map, and the branch ships with **no admin check** while every existing test stays green — a permission hole opened by an omission. Now check 10, proven to fail in both directions *in isolation*: an ungated module prefix, and a gate entry the module has dropped. The first attempt at that proof was inconclusive and said so — the mutation tripped check 9 as well, and a non-zero exit is not evidence that the check being aimed at did anything.

**Check 9 is what makes the declaration worth trusting:** every branch literal must be covered by its own module's `OWNED_PREFIXES`, and every declared prefix must have at least one branch behind it. Checks 2, 7 and 10 all read the declaration while Discord routes on the branches — two pieces of state with nothing holding them together.

**One recommendation was retracted before it shipped, by reading the seven lines above the code.** The audit's first finding was that `colors.js` declares `OWNED_PREFIXES` and never reads it, and its proposed fix was to give it the `ownsCustomId()` the other twelve have. The comment directly above that declaration says it is **declarative only, on purpose**: gating on the prefix would swallow an unrecognised `colors_*` id rather than letting it fall through, changing the pre-split behaviour the split worked to preserve — and it would have broken check 4. What was real was the sentence ending that comment, *"Keep this list in step with the branches"*: an obligation on whoever edits the file, and now an assertion. The right answer to a documented manual obligation is to assert it, not to delete the thing it protects.

**Four false alarms, and a direction worth naming.** The `toggle_` collision chased earlier this evening was `drawprices.js`'s own comment explaining the prefix it deliberately avoided; 66 phantom cross-module collisions were all `typeof customId === 'string'`; 49 "silent" catch blocks came from a brace walk that never entered the body (0 of 54 are silent); four "unreachable" modals were template heads compared in one direction. Every one was a **false alarm rather than a false clean** — the mirror image of this split's earlier sweeps, which reported clean before they were. A false alarm costs a verification round; a false clean ships a bug. Both are defects in the instrument, only one is dangerous, and a check added to the suite has to keep its failures on the alarm side.

**What came back clean, recorded because a clean result from a check nobody had run is worth as much as a finding.** The producer-derived corpus — 131 distinct minted ids across `commands/`, `utils/`, `handlers/` and `bot/`, the id set built from where ids are *created* rather than where they are matched — has **zero orphans**; the 40 apparent misses are modal text-input fields, confirmed read through `fields.getTextInputValue()`. Require **cycles**, which "all 171 paths resolve" cannot detect, number exactly one — `utils/adminAccess.js` ↔ `commands/manage.js` — and all three of its edges are lazy `require`s inside functions, so nothing sees a half-built `{}` at module-eval time. The seven module-level `Map` stores are each touched by exactly one file, so the split did not hand two subsystems separate instances of a store they used to share. And actual branch literals — not just declared prefixes — are mutually exclusive across all fourteen modules, which is the stronger form of the property the dispatch chain's own comment asserts.

**The whole branch diff was finally read end to end, by making it small enough to read.** 85 files, 6,030 insertions, 4,689 deletions — the standing reason nobody had done it. But a pure-move refactor does not need reading, it needs *comparing*: partitioning the diff into lines that appear on both sides (a move) and lines that appear on only one (genuinely new or genuinely lost) leaves **3,760 of 4,339 deleted lines accounted for as exact moves**. Normalising the one mechanical rewrite the split is known to have made — `require('./x')` → `require('../x')`, forced by moving files one level down — takes it to **3,934**, and collapses the deleted-only non-comment residue to **73 lines**. Those 73 fit on one screen and every one is explicable: the destructured `discord.js` import block (now in `bot/`), 19 `client.commands.get(…)` reads (now `interaction.client.commands`), the eight bare `return;`s that became the boolean contract's `return true/false`, and the branch conditions that gained an interaction-type test. Nothing was lost. **The lesson is that "too big to read" was a property of how the diff was being looked at, not of the diff.**

**The cooldowns and the concurrency are now tested rather than asserted** — `scripts/handlerState.test.js`, 7 checks. The previous claim was that each store "lives in exactly one module", which proves *one instance exists* and says nothing about whether the timing works. It needs no Discord and no Mongo, and that falls out of the code rather than a mock pile: `attachGuildPolicy` returns immediately when `guildId` is null, `resolvePanelActor` returns immediately when the panel's target is the clicker, and past the cooldown a handler's first act is `deferUpdate()` — so a mock whose `deferUpdate` throws a sentinel stops execution exactly after the store is written and before any database work, which is what makes "the cooldown accepted this click" observable. It covers the 10s Refresh-Colors cooldown and the generic 600ms anti-spam guard: rejection, per-user keying, window expiry (a throttle, not a latch), and **two simultaneous clicks resolving to exactly one**. That last one passes only because the read, the comparison and the write sit in one synchronous run; inserting a single `await` between them makes both clicks pass, and the test says so. Five mutations, five caught by the intended check — including one first attempt that was **wrong rather than reassuring**: a "global key" mutation that broke read/write symmetry tripped a different assertion, so it was rewritten to change both the read and the write before it counted.

**Three gaps found in that audit were closed rather than carried.** The `/manage` admin gate was scoped to three interaction types while the `/server` dispatcher fifteen lines above covers five — **the type test is now gone entirely**, because the prefix match is what selects the guarded set and the type list only supplied a way to fall out of scope. `handlers/alerts.js`, which carried no type predicate at all, gained one per branch. And `scripts/reflow-prose.mjs --check` **exited 0 on "would change"**, so CLAUDE.md's standing claim that a hard-wrapped paragraph fails the suite was false — the gate printed into a green run and blocked nothing, with one file hard-wrapped underneath it.

**One thing was deliberately NOT fixed, on a measurement.** Seven other handlers also carry zero type tests, and making that an offence would have meant seven speculative guards on a merging PR. Deriving each module's minted component types from its construction sites and matching them against its declared prefixes shows every zero-test module is single-type — `colors`/`drawprices`/`pagination` BUTTON-only, `help`/`patchnotes` STRING_SELECT-only — while both genuinely multi-type modules already test. The invariant that matters is *"a module whose prefixes carry more than one minted type must type-test"*, not *"every module must type-test"*. No check was added for it either: the type detection resolves 8 of 13 modules, and one blind to the other five would pass vacuously, which is worse than a recorded measurement.

**Verify:** `npm test` (exit 0 — the routing-contract suite alone is 50 assertions over 13 handlers, plus 7 state checks) · `npm run docs:audit` (exit 0, 40 of 41; the skip is `archive-conservation`, which needs `--diff <base>` because conservation is a fact about a change and cannot be read from the tree). *This line previously read "70 chained cases", a count no current measurement reproduces — the run reports 145 ✓ in total, 69 from the docs-audit self-test, 50 routing, 26 hooks. Adding three checks to the suite is what exposed it: a bare total in prose has no owner and nothing recomputes it, which is why the numbers here now name what they count.* **Not deployed** — pre-release work on `v3-pre-release`; the VM still runs `main`.

## Pre-Release v3.15.0 — 2026-08-13 15:41 EDT (#123 · `566b3ca`) — admin access becomes per-page, announcements become a real queue

Three items bundled by scheduling, not design overlap — each built, tested, and verified independently.

**`/colors` gains a landing option.** A `page` string-choice reordered ahead of `source`/`visibility` (Discord's option picker follows registration order, not alphabetical) jumps straight to Avatar/Banner/Name/Nameplate/Deco instead of always opening on Avatar. `from` was renamed `source` with clearer choice labels ("From Main Profile"/"From Server Profile") in the same pass.

**Multi-user admin access is scoped per-PAGE within `/manage`, not just per top-level command.** A token vocabulary (`all` / `manage` / `alerts` / `autobuild` / `manage.<page>`, `utils/adminAccess.js`) lets the owner grant a trusted person exactly the `/manage` pages they need — e.g. Calendar only — rather than all-or-nothing `/manage` access. Enforced at every command guard, the shared button/modal prefix guard (previously one blanket check covering `/manage`+`/alerts`+`/autobuild` together — a real gap, since it meant an `/alerts`-only grant could still click `/manage`'s own buttons), and `/help`'s Bot Admin category, which now filters each command line individually. Manage Admins stays owner-only visibility — never grantable at any scope. Rich per-admin cards show a live avatar thumbnail, clickable mention, raw Discord ID, formatted permissions and note, with Edit Permissions (reopens prefilled, add/remove by editing the list) and Revoke directly on each card.

**Announcement was rebuilt twice the same day.** The first version was a singleton (`docType: 'global'`) that silently lost data — posting a second announcement before a user saw the first overwrote it entirely, and there was no way to delete just one. It's now a real collection: one doc per announcement, per-user `seenAnnouncementIds` tracking instead of a single version number. Delivery bundles every unseen announcement into ONE ephemeral follow-up as separate embeds (never one message per announcement), each with a random-but-constrained-HSL accent colour generated once at creation and never regenerated on edit. Expiry defaults to 60 days, accepts a custom day count or `never`, filtered at query time in both delivery and the `/manage` list — no cleanup job needed.

Two real bugs found by direct reproduction against the dev DB, not by reading code: a `manageCommand` reference living outside the block scope where it was declared, and a stale MongoDB unique index (`docType_1`) surviving the Announcement singleton→collection schema rewrite — both produced a silent "stuck" interaction (`deferReply` acknowledged, nothing ever resolved it) rather than a visible error, since neither exception was caught locally and both fell through to the outer crash-safety handler. A real regression in `guildPolicyEnforcement.test.js`'s Bot Admin test fixture (missing the new per-command permission keys) was also caught and fixed before merge.

`docs/legal/PRIVACY.md` gained §2.1b and Appendix A entries for the two new records (`AdminUser`, `Announcement`) and the new `UserPreference.seenAnnouncementIds` field — folded into the existing pending v1.11 entry rather than a new version number, since all of it ships together on the v3 release.

## Pre-Release v3.14.0 — 2026-08-13 10:12 EDT (#122 · `2b31770`) — an invisible pixel stops passing for an opaque one

**Harkirat felt View Colors' panel switching and cold-start renders had gotten slightly less snappy, and asked for real data instead of three inconsistent manual timings.** Built durable instrumentation (`models/RenderTiming.js`) and let it accumulate through real dev-bot use. **Neither complaint held up**: 73 real panel-switch samples show no systematic slowdown (`subpage/avatar`'s clearest series actually trends faster across the session, not slower), and a purpose-built harness that forces repeated cold renders of the same nameplate/decoration design (bypassing the panel, no gateway login needed — `uploadToStorageChannel` only ever required `BOT_TOKEN`) found the same: 13 forced-plus-organic cold renders per source settle into a stable band with essentially zero drift.

**While identifying the investigation's own test image, a real bug turned up.** The corpus avatar at the center of it (`cinnasip.png`) was producing a phantom `#071948` "accent" swatch with no visible source in the picture. Confirmed by direct pixel scan: the handful of pixels near that hex sit at alpha 1–2 out of 255 — about 99.6% transparent, invisible to any viewer. `colorExtract.js`'s pixel samplers had only ever skipped `alpha === 0` exactly (the fix from the original 2026-07-14 transparency bug), so near-zero-but-nonzero alpha still counted at full RGB strength. Widened to `ALPHA_FLOOR = 13` (~5% opacity) — deliberately conservative, since the corpus's partial-alpha pixels form a smooth antialiasing ramp with no natural gap to derive a threshold from.

**Verified over 401 corpus images, matched by nearest colour rather than list position** (position alone can't tell a real colour shift from harmless reordering): only 4 palettes changed at all, total swatch count unchanged, and accent-origin swatches barely moved — a net gain, not a loss. Checked all 4 individually for a genuinely tiny real colour getting silently dropped: none did. Two were pure reordering with zero actual colour difference; one had two nudges just under the "same colour" threshold; `cinnasip.png`'s changed entries were exactly the phantom-bug-contaminated cluster merging into one honest, real swatch.

**Verify:** `npm test` (69 chained cases, unchanged) · `npm run docs:audit` (41/41) · `local/colors-investigation/alpha-floor-verify.mjs` for the corpus diff.
